1.1: In the first times the Lord created the heavens and the earth.
1.2: And the earth was waste and empty, and darkness was upon the face of the abyss; and a wind from before the Lord blew upon the face of the waters.
1.3: And the Lord said, Let there be light; and there was light.
1.4: And the Lord saw the light that it was good. And the Lord distinguished between the light and between the darkness.
1.5: And the Lord called the light the Day, and the darkness He called the Night. And there was evening, and there was morning, Day the First.
1.6: And the Lord said, Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let it distinguish between waters and waters.
1.7: And the Lord made the expanse, and distinguished between the waters which were under the expanse, and between the waters which were above the expanse: and it was so.
1.8: And the Lord called the expanse the Heavens. And it was evening, and it was morning, the Second Day.
1.9: And the Lord said, The waters shall be collected under the heavens into one region, and the dry land shall appear. And it was so.
1.10: And the Lord called the dry land Earth, and the place of the collection of waters He called Sea. And the Lord saw that it was good.
1.11: And the Lord said, The earth shall bring forth grass; the plant whose germ-seed is to be sown; the fruit-tree making fruit according to its kind, whose germ-seed is in it upon the earth; and it was so.
1.12: And the earth put forth grass; the herb, whose germ-seed is sown after its kind; and the tree making fruit, whose seed is in it after its kind. And the Lord saw that it was good.
1.13: And it was evening, and it was morning, Day the Third.
1.14: And the Lord said, There shall be Lights in the expanse of heaven, to distinguish between the day and the night; and they shall be for signs and for times, for the numbering of days and years.
1.15: And they shall be for luminaries in the expanse of heaven to shine upon the earth; and it was so.
1.16: And the Lord made the two great luminaries: the greater luminary to rule in the day; and the smaller luminary to rule in the night, and the stars.
1.17: And the Lord set them in the expanse of heaven to shine upon the earth,
1.18: and to rule in the day and in the night, and to distinguish between light and darkness. And the Lord saw that it was good.
1.19: And there was evening, and there was morning, Day the Fourth.
1.20: And the Lord said, Let the waters generate the moving creature (having) life; and the fowl which flieth over the earth on the face of the expanse of heaven.
1.21: And the Lord created the great taninia and every living animal which moveth, which the waters generated according to their kind, and every fowl which flieth according to his kind; and the Lord saw that it was good.
1.22: And the Lord blessed them, saying, Spread abroad and become many, and fill the waters of the seas; and let the fowl become many on the earth.
1.23: And it was evening, and it was morning, Day the Fifth.
1.24: And the Lord said, Let the earth produce the living animal after its kind, cattle, and reptile, and beast of the earth, according to its kind; and it was so.
1.25: And the Lord mad, the beast of the earth after its kind, and cattle after their kind, and every reptile of the earth after its kind; and the Lord saw that it was good.
1.26: And the Lord said, Let us make Man in Our image, as Our likeness; and shall have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heavens, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every reptile which moveth upon the earth.
1.27: And the Lord created the Adam in His image, in the image of the Lord He created him; male and female He created them.
1.28: And the Lord blessed them, and said to them, spread abroad, and become many, and fill the earth, and be strong upon it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heavens, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
1.29: And the Lord said, Behold, I have given to you every plant which seedeth green-seed which is upon all the earth; and every tree in which is the fruit of the tree which seedeth germ-seed; unto you it shall be for food,
1.30: and unto every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the heavens, and to every reptile upon the earth in which is the breath of life, every green herb to eat; and it was so.
1.31: And the Lord saw all that He had made, and, behold, it was very steadfast. And it was evening, and it was morning, Day the Sixth.

2.1: And the heavens and the earth and all their host were completed.
2.2: And the Lord finished in the Seventh Day His work which He had wrought, and rested in the Seventh Day from all His work which He had wrought.
2.3: And the Lord blessed the Seventh Day and made it holy, because in it He rested from all His work which the Lord had created to make.
2.4: These are the memorials of the heavens and the earth, when they were created in the day when the Lord God made the earth and the heavens.
2.5: And all trees of the field were not yet in the earth, and every herb of the field had not yet sprung up, because the Lord God had not caused rain to come upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.
2.6: And a mist ascended from the earth, and moistened all the face of the ground.
2.7: And the Lord God created Adam from dust of the ground, and breathed upon his face the breath of lives, and it became in Adam a Discoursing Spirit.
2.8: And the Lord God planted a garden in a region of pleasantness in the time of the beginning, and He made to dwell there the man whom He had created.
2.9: And the Lord God caused to grow from the earth every tree desirable to look upon, and good for food, and the Tree of Life (Lives) in the midst of the garden, and the Tree of whose fruit they who eat know between good and evil.
2.10: And a river went forth from Eden to water the garden, and from thence it was divided and became four heads of rivers (or four chief rivers).
2.11: The name of the first is Pishon, that which encompasseth all the land of Havilah, where is gold;
2.12: and the gold of that land is good; there is bedalcha and Burilla stones.
2.13: And the name of the second river is Gichon, which encompasseth all the land of Kush.
2.14: And the name of the third river is Digelatlh, which goeth to the east of Athur. And the fourth river is Pherat.
2.15: And the Lord God took Adam and placed him in the garden of Eden to culture it and keep it.
2.16: And the Lord God commanded Adam, saying, Of every tree of the garden eating thou mayest eat;
2.17: but of the tree of whose fruit they who eat know between good and evil thou shalt not eat; for in the day that thou eatest of it dying thou shalt die.
2.18: And the Lord God said, It is not right that Adam should be solitary; I will make for him a helper as for his sake (or, as suited to him: Heb., kenegdo, as his counterpart).
2.19: And the Lord God created from the earth every beast of the field and every fowl of the heavens, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call him; and every (name by) which Adam called the living animal, that was its name.
2.20: And Adam called the name of all cattle, and of the fowl of the heaven, and of every beast of the field; but to Adam was not found a helper as for him.
2.21: And the Lord God threw a sleep upon Adam, and he slept; and He took one of his ribs, and filled with flesh in place thereof;
2.22: and the Lord God builded the rib which He took from Adam into Woman, and He brought her unto Adam.
2.23: And Adam said, This now (this time) is bone of my bone, and flesh of my flesh: this shall be called Woman, because from her husband this was taken.
2.24: Therefore shall a man forsake the couch (beth mishkeb, the sleeping-house) of his father and his mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they shall be of one flesh.
2.25: And they were both naked, Adam and his wife, and were not ashamed.

3.1: And the serpent (chivja) was more crafty than all the animals of the field which the Lord God bad made. And he said to the woman, Is it in truth (that) the Lord said, You shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
3.2: And the woman said to the serpent, Of the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat;
3.3: but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, the Lord hath said, You shall not eat of it, nor approach to it, lest you die.
3.4: And the serpent said to the woman. Not to die will you die:
3.5: for it is manifest before the Lord, that in the day in which you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be (ki-rabrebin) as the Great-ones, knowing good and evil.
3.6: And the woman saw that the tree was good to eat, and that it was salutary to the eyes, and a tree desirable to contemplate; and she took of its fruitage (aiba) and ate; and she gave to her husband with her, and he ate.
3.7: And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed for themselves the leaves of the fig tree, and made for themselves cinctures.
3.8: And they heard the voice of the Word of the Lord God walking in the garden in the evening of the day; and Adam and his wife hid themselves from before the Lord God among the trees of the garden.
3.9: And the Lord God called to Adam and said to him, Where art thou?
3.10: And he said, The voice of Thy Word heard I in the garden, and I was afraid, because I (was) naked, and I would hide.
3.11: And He said, Who showed thee that thou wast naked? Of the tree of which I commanded that eating of it thou shouldst not eat, hast thou eaten?
3.12: And Adam said, The woman whom Thou gavest (to be) with me, she gave to me of the tree, and I did eat.
3.13: And the Lord God said to the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent led me astray, and I did eat.
3.14: And the Lord God said to the serpent, Because thou hast done this, more accursed art thou than all cattle, and than all the beasts of the held; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and the dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life.
3.15: And I will put enmity between thee and between the woman, and between thy son and her son. He will remember thee, what thou didst to him (at) from the beginning, and thou shalt be observant unto him at the end.
3.16: And to the woman He said, Multiplying, I will multiply thy sorrows and thy pains. In sorrow shalt thou bring forth children; and unto thy husband shall be thy desire, and lie. He shall rule over thee.
3.17: And unto Adam He said, Because thou hast obeyed the word of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree (about) which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it, accursed is the ground on thy account. With labour shalt thou eat from it all the days of thy life.
3.18: Thorns and thistles it shall put forth for thee, and thou shalt eat the herb of the field.
3.19: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, until that thou return to the earth, because from it thou wast created; for dust thou art, and to dust thou wilt return.
3.20: And Adam called the name of his wife Hava, because she was the mother of all the children of men.
3.21: And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife vestments of honor upon the skin of their flesh, and clothed them.
3.22: And the Lord God said, Behold, man is become singular (or alone, yechid) in the world by himself, knowing good and evil; and now, lest he stretch forth his hand and take also of the Tree of Life, and eat, and live forever.
3.23: And the Lord God sent him forth from the Garden of Eden to till the ground from whence he had been created.
3.24: And He drove out the man, and before the garden of Eden he caused to dwell the kerubaya, and the sharp sword which revolved to keep the way of the Tree of Life.

4.1: And Adam knew Hava his wife, and she conceived, and gave birth to Kain; and she said I have acquired the man from before the Lord.
4.2: And she added to give birth to his brother, Habel. And Habel was a shepherd of the flock, and Kain a man working on the ground.
4.3: And it was at the end (or complement) of days, that Kain brought of the product of the earth an oblation before the Lord;
4.4: and Habel he brought also of the first-born of his sheep and of their fatlings. And there was acceptableness before the Lord in Habel and in his oblation;
4.5: but in Kain and his oblation there was not acceptableness. And it was greatly displeasing to Kain, and his countenance was downcast.
4.6: And the Lord said to Kain, Why art thou displeased, and why is thy countenance downcast?
4.7: If thou doest thy work well, is it not remitted to thee? And if thou doest not thy work well, thy sin unto the day of judgment is reserved, when it will be exacted of thee, if thou convert not: but if thou convert, it is remitted to thee.
4.8: And Kain spake with Habel his brother; and it was in their being in the field that Kain arose against Habel his brother, and killed him.
4.9: And the Lord said to Kain, Where is Habel thy brother? And he said, I know not; am I the keeper of my brother?
4.10: And He said, What hast thou done? The voice of the blood of generations which were to come from thy brother complaineth before Me, from the earth!
4.11: And now, accursed art thou from the earth, which hath opened her mouth and received the blood of thy brother from thy hand.
4.12: When thou tillest the earth, it shall not add to give its virtue to thee; a castaway and a wanderer shalt thou be in the earth.
4.13: And Kain said before the Lord, Greater is my guilt than may be forgiven.
4.14: Behold, Thou hast rejected me this day from the face of the earth, and from Thy presence it is not possible to hide; and I shall be a castaway and a wanderer in the earth, and anyone who findeth me will slay me.
4.15: And the Lord said to him, Therefore anyone who killeth Kain, unto seven generations it shall be exacted of him. And the Lord set unto Kain a sign, lest anyone who found him should kill him.
4.16: And Kain went out from before the Lord, and dwelt in the land of the wanderer and outcast, which was made for him in the beginnings in the Garden of Eden.
4.17: And Kain knew his wife, and she conceived and bare Hanoch, and he became the builder of a city, and called the name of the city after the name of his son Hanoch.
4.18: And there was born to Hanoch Irad, and Irad begat Mahujael; and Mahujael begat Methu-sael, and Methusael begat Lemek.
4.19: And Lemek took unto him two wives, the name of the one Ada, and the name of the second Zillah.
4.20: And Ada bare Javal; he was the master (rab) of all dwellers in tents and lords of cattle.
4.21: And the name of his brother was Juval. He was the master of all who play upon the mouth of the pipe, who know the song of the harp and of the organ.
4.22: And Zillah also, she bare Tuval-kain, the master of all them who understand the working of brass and iron. And the sister of Tuval-kain was Naamah.
4.23: And Lemek said to his wives Ada and Zillah, Hear my voice, wives of Lemek, attend to my words: I have not slain a man, that on his account I should bear the condemnation of death; or destroyed a young man, that on his account my posterity should be consumed.
4.24: If seven generations are suspended unto Kain, will there not be to Lemek his son seventy and seven?
4.25: And Adam knew yet his wife, and she bare a son, and called his name Sheth; Because, said she, the Lord hath given me another son instead of Habel, whom Kain slew.
4.26: And to Sheth also was born a son, and he called his name Enosh. Then in his days the sons of men desisted (or forbore) from praying in the name of the Lord.

5.1: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that the Lord God created man, in the resemblance of Elohim He made him;
5.2: Male and female He created them; and He blessed them, and called their name Man, in the day that they were created.
5.3: And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begat in his resemblance (one) who was like to himself, and he called his name Sheth.
5.4: And the days of Adam after he had begotten Sheth were eight hundred years, and be begat sons and daughters.
5.5: And all the days of Adam which he lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
5.6: And Sheth lived a hundred and five years, and begat Enosh.
5.7: And Sheth lived after he had begotton Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.8: And all the days of Sheth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
5.9: And Enosh lived ninety years, and begat Keinan.
5.10: And Enosh lived after he had begotten Keinan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.11: And all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died.
5.12: And Keinan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalalel.
5.13: And Keinan lived after he had begotten Mahalalel eight hundred and forty years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.14: And all the days of Keinan were nine hundred and ten years, and be died.
5.15: And Mahalalel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jered.
5.16: And Mahalalel lived after he had begotten Jered eight hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.17: And all the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred and ninety and five years, and he died.
5.18: And Jered lived an hundred and sixty and two years, and begat Hanok.
5.19: And Jered lived after he had begotten Hanok eight hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.20: And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty and two years, and he died.
5.21: And Hanok lived sixty and five years, and begat Methushelach.
5.22: And Hanok walked in the fear of the Lord, after he had begotten Methushelach, three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.23: And all the days of Hanok were three hundred and sixty and five years.
5.24: And Hanok walked in the fear of the Lord; and he was not; for the Lord had not made him to die.
5.25: And Methushelach lived an hundred and eighty and seven years, and begat Lemek.
5.26: And Methushelach lived after he had begotten Lemek seven hundred and eighty and two years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.27: And all the days of Methushelach were nine hundred and sixty and nine years, and he died.
5.28: And Lemek lived a hundred and eighty and two years, and begat a son.
5.29: And he called his name Noach, saying, This shall console us from the works and from the labour of our hands from the earth which the Lord bath cursed.
5.30: And Lemek lived, after he had begotten Noach, five hundred and ninety and five years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.31: And all the days of Lemek were seven hundred and seventy and seven years, and he died.
5.32: And Noach was a son of five hundred years, and Noach begat Shem, Cham, and Japheth.

6.1: And it was when the sons of men had begun to multiply upon the earth, and daughters were born to them,
6.2: that the sons of the mighty saw the daughters of men that they were beautiful, and took to them wives of all whom they pleased.
6.3: And the Lord said, This evil generation shall not stand before me forever, because they are flesh, and their works are evil. A term (or length) will I give them, an hundred and twenty years, if they may be converted.
6.4: Giants were in the earth in those days; and also when, after that the sons of the mighty had gone in unto the daughters of men, there were born from them giants who from of old were men of name.
6.5: And the Lord saw that the wickedness of man had multiplied in the earth, and that every formation (or image) of the thought of his heart was only evil every day.
6.6: And it repented the Lord in His Word that He had made men upon the earth.
6.7: And He said, (in His Word,) that He would break their strength according to His pleasure. And the Lord said, Man whom I have made will I blot out I from the face of the earth; from man to the beast, to the reptile, and to the fowls of heaven; because it repenteth Me in My Word that I have made them.
6.8: But Noach found mercy before the Lord.
6.9: These are the memorials of Noach. Noach was a man righteous and perfect in his generation; in the fear of the Lord walked Noach.
6.10: And Noach begat three sons, Shem, Cham, and Yapeth.
6.11: And the earth was corrupted before the Lord, and the earth was filled with violences.
6.12: And the Lord saw the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt, because all flesh had corrupted, each one, his way upon the earth.
6.13: And the Lord said to Noach, The end of all flesh cometh before Me, because the earth is filled with violences from the face of their wicked works; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
6.14: Make thee an ark with the wood of cedar; dwellings shalt thou make in the ark, and overlay it within and without with pitch.
6.15: And thus shalt thou make it: three hundred cubits shall be the length of the ark, fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height.
6.16: A light shalt thou make to the ark, and at a cubit shalt thou complete it above, and the door of the ark thou shalt place in its side. Lower dwellings, second and third, shalt thou make in it.
6.17: And I, behold, I do bring the deluge of waters upon the earth to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life from under the heavens. Everything that is on the earth shall die.
6.18: And I will establish My covenant with thee; and thou shalt enter into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and the wives of thy sons with thee.
6.19: And of all that liveth of all flesh two and two of all that enter into the ark to abide with thee, male and female shall they be.
6.20: Of fowl according to its kind, and of cattle according to her kind, and of every creeping thing of the earth after his kind, two of all shall enter with thee to abide.
6.21: And thou, take with thee of all food which is eaten, and gather to be with thee; and it shall be for thee and for them to eat.
6.22: And Noach did according to all which the Lord had commanded him, so did he.

7.1: And the Lord said to Noach, Enter thou and all the men of thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before Me in this generation.
7.2: Of all clean animals take thou seven and seven, male and female; and of animals not clean, two and two, male and female.
7.3: Also of the fowls of heaven, seven and seven, male and female, to continue the seed upon the face of all the earth.
7.4: Because yet a time of seven days and I will cause rain to descend upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will blot out every subsistence which I have made upon all the face of the earth.
7.5: And Noach did according to all that the Lord had instructed him.
7.6: And Noach was a son of six hundred years; and the deluge of waters was upon the earth.
7.7: And Noach entered, and his sons, and his wife, and the wives of his sons with him, into the ark from before the water of the deluge.
7.8: Of animals clean, and of animals not clean, and of birds, and of all which creepeth upon the earth,
7.9: two and two, they entered with Noach into the ark, male and female, as the Lord had instructed Noach.
7.10: And it was at the time of seven days, and the waters of the deluge were upon the earth.
7.11: In the six-hundredth year of the life of Noach, in the second month, in the seven-teenth day of the month, in that day were all the springs of the great abyss upbroken, and the windows of heaven opened,
7.12: and the rain came down upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
7.13: In that very day entered Noach, and Shem, Cham, and Yapheth, sons of Noach, and the wife of Noach, and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark;
7.14: They, and every animal after his kind, and all cattle after its kind, and every, reptile which creepeth upon the earth after its kind, and every fowl after its kind, every bird, everyone that flieth:
7.15: And they entered with Noach into the ark, two and two of all flesh in which is the breath of life;
7.16: And they, entering, male and female of all flesh, entered, as the Lord had commanded him, and the Lord protected them by His Word.
7.17: And there was a deluge forty days upon the earth, and the waters increased, and took up the ark, and it was lifted up above the earth.
7.18: And the waters prevailed and increased mightily upon the earth, and the ark went upon the faces of the waters.
7.19: And the waters prevailed most mightily over the earth, and all the high hills were covered which were under all the heavens.
7.20: Fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail, and the mountains were covered;
7.21: And all flesh died which moved upon the earth, of fowl, and of cattle, and of the wild beast, and of every reptile which creepeth upon the earth, and every man.
7.22: Everything in whose nostrils was the breath of the Spirit of life, of all which was upon the dry ground, died.
7.23: And every subsistence was blotted out that was upon the faces of the earth, from man to the beast, to the reptile, and to the fowl of heaven, it was blotted out from the earth, and Noach was left alone, and they who were with him in the ark.
7.24: And the waters prevailed upon the earth an hundred and fifty days.

8.1: And the Lord remembered Noach, and every living thing, and all the cattle which were with him in the ark; and the Lord caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters rested,
8.2: and the springs of the abyss were shut, and the windows of the heavens, and the rain from the heavens was restrained, and the waters turned from on the earth, going and returning;
8.3: And the waters diminished from the end of a hundred and fifty days.
8.4: And the ark rested on the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Kardu.
8.5: And the waters went and diminished until the tenth month: in the tenth, on the first of the mouth, the heads of the mountains appeared.
8.6: And it was at the end of forty days, and Noach opened the windows of the ark which he had made.
8.7: And he sent forth a raven, and going he went out, and returned until the waters were dried upon the earth.
8.8: And he sent forth a dove from (being) with him, to see whether the waters were lightened (or consumed) from the surface of the earth.
8.9: But the dove found no rest for the dividing of her foot, and she returned unto him into the ark, because the waters were upon all the earth; and he stretched forth his hand, and took her, and brought her to be with him in the ark.
8.10: And he prolonged yet seven days, and afterward added to send forth the dove from the ark.
8.11: And the dove came to him at the time of evening, and, behold, a leaf of olive broken off was in her mouth; and Noach knew that the waters were lightened from upon the earth.
8.12: And he prolonged yet other seven days, and sent forth the dove, and she added not to return to be with him again.
8.13: And it was in the six-hundredth and first year, in the beginning of the first month, the waters were dried from off the earth; and Noach removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and, behold, the faces of the ground were dry.
8.14: And in the second month, in the seventeenth day of the month, the earth was fully dry.
8.15: And the Lord spake with Noach, saying:
8.16: Go forth from the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and the wives of thy sons with thee.
8.17: Every living thing which is with thee of all flesh, of fowl, and of cattle, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth, bring forth with thee, and they shall generate in the earth, and spread abroad and multiply upon the earth.
8.18: And Noach went forth, and his sons, and his wife, and the wives of his sons with him;
8.19: Every animal, every reptile and bird, everything which moveth upon the earth after their kind, went forth from the ark.
8.20: And Noach builded an altar before the Lord, and took of every clean beast and of every clean bird, and uplifted an offering upon the altar.
8.21: And the Lord received with approval his oblation; and the Lord said in His Word, I will not add to curse again the earth on account of the guilt of man, because the creations of the heart of man are evil from his infancy; and I will not add again to smite every living thing as I have done.
8.22: Yet all the days of the earth, seed-time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night, shall not cease.

9.1: And the Lord blessed Noach and his sons, and said to them, Spread abroad, and multiply, and fill the earth.
9.2: And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the heavens, in all which creepeth upon the earth, and in all fish of the sea; into your hands shall they be delivered.
9.3: Every moving thing that liveth, for you it shall be to eat; as the green herb I have given you the whole.
9.4: But the flesh with its life-blood you shall not eat.
9.5: And also your blood of your lives will I require, from every beast will I require it, and from the hand of man. From the hand of the man who sheddeth the blood of his brother will I require the life of man.
9.6: Whoso sheddeth the blood of man, by witnesses, upon the sentence of the judges, his blood shall be shed; because in the image of the Lord made He man.
9.7: And you, spread abroad and multiply; bring forth in the earth and multiply therein.
9.8: And the Lord spake to Noach, and to his sons with him, saying,
9.9: and I, behold, I establish my covenant with you and with your children after you,
9.10: and with every living thing which is with you, of fowl, of cattle, and of every beast of the field that is with you, of all going forth from the ark of every animal of the earth.
9.11: And I will establish My covenant with you, and all flesh shall not again be consumed by the waters of a deluge, nor shall there be again a deluge to destroy the earth.
9.12: And the Lord said, This is the sign of the covenant which I appoint (give) between My Word, and between you, and between every living soul that is with you unto perpetual generations.
9.13: I have set My bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of the covenant between My Word and between the earth.
9.14: And it shall be that when clouding I becloud the earth, the bow shall be seen in the cloud,
9.15: and I will remember the covenant which is between My Word, and between You, and between every living soul of all flesh; and there shall not be again the waters of a deluge to destroy all flesh.
9.16: And the bow shall be in the cloud, and I will look upon it, to remember the everlasting covenant between the Word of the Lord and between every living soul of all flesh that is upon the earth.
9.17: And the Lord said, This is the sign of the covenant which I have established between My Word and between all flesh which is upon the earth.
9.18: And the sons of Noach who went forth from the ark were Shem and Cham and Yapheth: and Cham is the father of Kenaan.
9.19: These three are the sons of Noach and from them was the whole earth Overspread.
9.20: And Noach began to be a man working on the earth; and he planted a vineyard,
9.21: and he drank of the wine, and was drunk; and he was uncovered in the midst of his tent.
9.22: And Cham the father of Kenaan saw the nakedness of his father, and he showed to his two brethren without.
9.23: And Shem and Yapheth took a mantle, and laid it upon the shoulders of both, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were averted, and the nakedness of their father they saw not.
9.24: And Noach awoke from his wine, and knew that which his youngest son had done unto him;
9.25: and he said; Accursed be Kenaan, A working servant shall he be to his brethren.
9.26: And he said: Blessed be the Lord the God of Shem, And Kenaan shall be servant unto them.
9.27: The Lord shall enlarge Yapheth, And He shall make his Shekinah to dwell in the tabernacles of Shem: And Kenaan shall be servant unto them.
9.28: And Noach lived after the deluge three hundred and fifty years.
9.29: And all the days of Noach were nine hundred and fifty years; and he died.

10.1: And these are the generations of the sons of Noach, Shem, Cham, and Yapheth; and sons were born to them after the deluge.
10.2: The sons of Yepheth, Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Yavan, and Thuval, and Meshek, and Tiras.
10.3: And the sons of Gomer, Ashkenaz, and Rephath, and Thogarmah.
10.4: And the sons of Yavan, Elishah and Tharshish, and Dodanim.
10.5: From these were the isles (nagvath) of the peoples divided in their lands, each according to his language, according to their families in their nations.
10.6: And the sons of Cham, Kush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Kenaan.
10.7: And the sons of Kush, Seba, and Chavilah, and Sabetha, and Raamah, and Sabtekah. And the sons of Raamah, Sheba and Dedan.
10.8: And Kush begat Nimrod: he began to be a powerful man in the earth.
10.9: He was a powerful man before the Lord: therefore it is said, Like Nimrod the man of might before the Lord.
10.10: And the head (beginning) of his kingdom was Bavel, and Erek, and Akad, and Kalneh in the land of Bavel.
10.11: From that land he went forth to Athura, and built Nineveh, and the city of Rechov, and Kalach,
10.12: and Resen, between Nineveh and Kalach, which was a great city.
10.13: And Mizraim begat the Ludaee, and Anamaee, and Lehabaee, and Naphtuhaee,
10.14: and Pathrusaee, and Kasluchaee, from whom came forth the Pelishtaee and Kaputkaee.
10.15: And Kenaan begat Zidon his firstborn, and Cheth,
10.16: and the Jebusaee, and Amoraee, and Girgashee,
10.17: and Hivaaee, and Arkaee, and Antasaee,
10.18: and Arvadaee, and Zemaraee, and Chamathaee: and afterwards the seed of the Kenaanaee were scattered abroad.
10.19: And the frontier of Kenaanaah was from Zidon, coming to Gerar and to Azza, coming unto Sedom, and Amorah, and Admah, and Zeboim, unto Lasha.
10.20: These are the sons of Cham, according to their progenies, to their languages, in their lands, in their peoples.
10.21: And of Shem was born: (also he is the father of all the sons of Eber, and the brother of Yapheth the Great:)
10.22: The sons of Shem, Elim, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
10.23: And the sons of Aram, Uz, and Chul, and Gether, and Mash.
10.24: And Arphaxad begat Shelach; and Shelach begat Eber.
10.25: And to Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg: because in his day the earth was divided. And the name of his brother was Yoktan.
10.26: And Yoktan begat Almodad, and Shaleph, and Chatsarmaveth, and Yarech,
10.27: and Chadoram, and Uzal, and Dikelah,
10.28: and Obal, and Avimael, and Sheba,
10.29: and Ophir, and Chavilah, and Yobab: all these are the sons of Yoktan.
10.30: And their dwelling was from Mesha, coming to Sephar, an eastern mountain.
10.31: These are the sons of Shem, according to their progenies, according to their languages, in their lands, in their peoples.
10.32: These are the progenies of the sons of Noach, by their generations, in their peoples: and by them were the peoples outspread in the earth after the deluge.

11.1: And all the earth was of one language and one speech.
11.2: And it was in their migrations at the beginning, that they found a plain in the land of Babel; and dwelt there.
11.3: And they said, a man to his companion, Come, let us cast bricks and bake them in the fire. And they had brick for stone, and bitumen for mortar.
11.4: And they said, Come, let us build a city, and a tower, the bead of it coming to the pinnacle of the heavens. And we will make to us a name, lest we be dispersed upon the face of all the earth.
11.5: And the Lord was revealed to punish the work of the city and the tower which the sons of men had builded.
11.6: And the Lord said, Behold, the people are one and the language one with all of them: and this is what they begin to do. And now nothing will be restrained from them of what they imagine to do.
11.7: Come, We will be manifest, and will confuse their language there, that a man shall not bear the language of his companion.
11.8: And the Lord dispersed them from thence upon the face of all the earth, and they were restrained from building the city.
11.9: Therefore the name of it is called Confusion, because the Lord there confused the tongue of all the earth, and from thence the Lord dispersed them upon the face of all the earth.
11.10: These are the generations of Shem. Shem was a son of a hundred years, and he begat Arphaxad, two years after the deluge.
11.11: And Shem lived after he had begotten Arphaxad five hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.12: And Arphaxad lived thirty and five years, and begat Shelach.
11.13: And Arphaxad lived after he had begotten Shelach four hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.14: And Shelach lived thirty years, and begat Eber.
11.15: And Shelach lived after he had begotten Eber four hundred and three years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.16: And Eber lived thirty and four years, and begat Peleg.
11.17: And Eber lived after he had begotten Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.18: And Peleg lived thirty years, and begat Reu.
11.19: And Peleg lived after he had begotten Reu two hundred and nine years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.20: And Reu lived thirty and two years, and begat Serug.
11.21: And Reu lived after he had begotten Serug two hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.22: And Serug lived thirty years, and begat Nachor.
11.23: And Serug lived after he had begotten Nachor two hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.24: And Nachor lived twenty and nine years, and begat Terach.
11.25: And Nachor lived after he had begotten Terach a hundred and nineteen years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.26: And Terach lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nachor, and Haran.
11.27: And these are the generations of Terach. Terach begat Abram, Nachor, and Haran; and Haran begat Lot.
11.28: And Haran died before Terach his father in the land of his nativity, in Ura of the Kasdaee.
11.29: And Abram and Nachor took to them wives: the name of the wife of Abram, Sara; and the name of the wife of Nachor, Milcha, daughter of Haran the father of Milcha and the father of Yiska.
11.30: And Sara was barren, she had no child.
11.31: And Terach took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran, the son of his son, and Sara his daughter-in-law, wife of Abram his son, and went forth with them from Ura of the Kasdaee to go to the land of Kenaan. And they came to Charan, and dwelt there.
11.32: And the days of Terach were two hundred and five years, and Terach died in Charan.

12.1: And the Lord said to ABRAM, Go thou away from thy country, and from the house of thy father, to the land which I will show thee.
12.2: And I will make thee to (be) a great people, and will bless thee, and magnify thy name, and thou shalt be blessed.
12.3: And I will bless him who blesseth thee, and him who curseth thee I will curse; and through thee all the progenies of the earth shall be blessed.
12.4: And Abram went away, according as the Lord had spoken to him, and Lot went with him. And Abram was a son of seventy and five years in his forthgoing from Charan.
12.5: And Abram took Sara his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all the possessions which they possessed, and the souls whom they had made subject to the law in Charan, and went forth to go into the land of Kenaan; and they came unto the land of Kenaan.
12.6: And Abram traversed through the land unto the place of Shekim unto the plain of Moreh; and the Kenaanah was then in the land.
12.7: And the Lord revealed Himself unto Abram, and said, To thy sons will I give this land. And he builded there an altar before the Lord who had been revealed to him.
12.8: And he ascended from thence to the mountain east of Beth El, and spread out his tabernacle, having Beth El on the west and Ai on the east; and he builded there an altar before the Lord, and prayed in the name of the Lord.
12.9: And Abram migrated, going and migrating to the south.
12.10: And there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Mizraim, to sojourn there, because the famine was strong in the land.
12.11: And it was that as he drew nigh to enter Mizraim he said to Sara his wife, Behold, now I know that thou art a woman beautiful in sight;
12.12: And it will be that when the Mizraee see thee they will say, This is his wife; and they will kill me, and thee will they reserve.
12.13: Say now, thou art my sister, that it may be well with me through thee, and my life may be preserved through thy words.
12.14: And it was that when Abram had entered into Mizraim, the Mizraee saw the woman that she was singularly fair;
12.15: And the princes of Pharaoh saw her, and extolled her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken to the house of Pharaoh.
12.16: And Abram was well treated on account of her. And he had sheep, and oxen, and asses, and servants, and maidens, and camels.
12.17: And the Lord brought upon Pharaoh great plagues, and upon the men of his house, for the affair of Sara the wife of Abram.
12.18: And Pharaoh called Abram and said, What is this that thou hast done to me? Why didst thou not show me that she is thy wife?
12.19: Why saidst thou, She is my sister, so that I would have taken her to me to wife? And now, behold thy wife: take, and go.
12.20: And Pharaoh instructed the men concerning him, and they, conducted him away, and his wife, and all that he had.

13.1: And Abram went up from Mizraim, he and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, unto the south.
13.2: And Abram was exceeding strong in cattle, in silver, and in gold;
13.3: And he proceeded according to his encampments from the south, and unto Bethel, unto the place where he had spread his tabernacle at the first, between Bethel and Ai;
13.4: To the place of the altar which he had there made at the first: and Abram prayed there in the Name of the Lord.
13.5: And Lot also, who went with Abram, had sheep and oxen and tents.
13.6: And the land could not support them, that they might dwell together.
13.7: And there was contention between the shepherds of the flock of Abram and the shepherds of the flock of Lot; and the Kenaanah and: the Pherizaah then dwelt in the land.
13.8: And Abram said to Lot, Let there not now be contention between me and thee, and between my shepherds and thy shepherds; for men, brethren, are we.
13.9: Is not all the land before thee? Separate now from me: if thou to the north, I to the south; and if thou to the south, I to the north.
13.10: And Lot lifted up his eyes, and saw all the plain of Yardena that it was altogether a watered place, before the Lord had destroyed Sedom and Amorah, as the garden of the Lord, as the land of Mizraim coming unto Zoar.
13.11: And Lot chose to him all the plain of Yardena; and Lot went forth before, and they were separated each man from his brother.
13.12: Abram dwelt in the land of Kenaan, and Lot dwelt in the cities of the plain, and extended unto Sedom.
13.13: And the men of Sedom were wicked in their riches, and guilty in their bodies before the Lord greatly.
13.14: And the Lord said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him, Lift up now thine eyes and see, from the place where thou art, thence to the north and to the south, and to the east and to the west;
13.15: For all this land that thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy children forever.
13.16: And I will place thy children numerous as the dust of the earth; so that as it is not possible for a man to number the dust of the earth, so also thy sons shall not be numbered.
13.17: Arise, go through the land, in its length and in its breadth; for unto thee will I give it.
13.18: And Abram spread (his tent), and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre which is near Hebron, and builded there an altar before the Lord.

14.1: And it was in the days of Amraphel, king of Babel, Ariok, king of Elasar, Kedar-laomer, king of Elam, and Thidal, king of peoples,
14.2: they made war with Bera, king of Sedom, and with Birsha, king of Amora, Shenab, king of Admah, Shemeber, king of Zeboim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
14.3: All these were assembled at the plain of the field, which is (now) the place of the sea of salt.
14.4: Twelve years they had served Kedar-laomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
14.5: And in the fourteenth year came Kedar-laomer, and the kings who were with him, and smote the giants who were in Ashtaroth Karnaim, and the mighty who were in Chemta, and the terrible ones who were in Shaveh Kiryathaim,
14.6: and the Horaee who were in the mountain of Seir, unto the plain of Paran which lieth upon the desert.
14.7: And they turned, and came to the plain of the division of judgment, which is Rekam, and smote all the fields of the Amalkaah, and also the Amoraah who dwelt in Ein-gadey.
14.8: And the king of Sedom, and the king of Amoraah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboim, and tile king of Bela, which is Zoar, went forth and set the battle in array against them in the plain of the field,
14.9: with Kedar-laomer king of Elam, and Thidal, king of peoples, and Amraphel, king of Babel, and Ariok, king of Elasar; four kings against five.
14.10: And the plain of the field had many pits, from which, they raised asphalta; and the kings of Sedom and Amorah fled, and they fell there; and they who remained fled to the mountain.
14.11: And they took all the possession of Sedom and Amorah, and, all their food, and went.
14.12: And they captured Lot and his substance, son of the brother of Abram, and went. And he had dwelt in Sedom.
14.13: And (one) came from those escaped, and showed to Abram the Ivraah; and he had remained in the plain of Moreh Amoraah, the brother of Eshkol and brother of Aner; and they were Abram’s men of covenant.
14.14: And Abram heard that his brother had been captured; and he armed the young men born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued unto Dan.
14.15: And he divided against them by night, he and his servants, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hoba, which was northward of Damasek.
14.16: And he recovered all the substance, and Lot also, the son of his brother; and his substance he recovered, the women also, and the people.
14.17: And the king of Sedom came out to meet him after returning from the smiting of Kedar-laomer and the kings who were with him, at the plain of Mephana, which was the king’s place of racing.
14.18: And Malki-zedek, king of Yerushelem, brought forth bread and wine (chemar), and he was minister (meshamesh) before EL ILLAAH,
14.19: and he blessed him, and said: “Blessed be Abram before El Illah, Whose possession is heaven and earth;
14.20: And blessed be El Illah (Most High), Who hath delivered thine enemies into thine hand.” And he gave him one in ten of the whole.
14.21: And the king of Sedom said to Abram, Give me the souls, and the substance take thou.
14.22: And Abram said to the king of Sedom, I have uplifted my hands in prayer before the Lord God most high, whose possession is heaven and earth:
14.23: If from a thread unto the sole of a sandal I take of all that is thine, (and not that thou shouldst say, I have enriched Abram,)
14.24: except of the food for the young men, and the share of the men who went with me, Amer, Eshkol, and Mamre, these will receive their shares.

15.1: After these things the word (pithgama) of the Lord came to Abram in prophecy, saying, Fear not, Abram: My Word (Memra) shall be thy strength, and thy exceeding great reward.
15.2: And Abram said, Lord God, what wilt Thou give me, and I go without a child: and this son of business (bar phargama) who is in My house is the Damasekah Elieser?
15.3: And Abram said, Behold, Thou hast not given me a child, and, behold, the son of my house is my heir.
15.4: And, lo, the word (pithgama) of the Lord was with him, saying, This shall not be thy heir, but a son whom thou shalt beget will be thine heir.
15.5: And He led him without, and said, Behold now the heavens, and number the stars, if thou art able to number them; and He said to him, So will be thy sons.
15.6: And he believed in the Word of the Lord, (Memra da Yeya,) and He reckoned it to him unto justification.
15.7: And He said to him, I am the Lord, who brought thee forth from Ura of the Kasdaee, to give thee this land to inherit it.
15.8: And he said, Lord God, by what may I know that I shall inherit it?
15.9: And He said to him, Bring Me three calves, and three goats, and three rams, and a turtle dove, and the young of a pigeon.
15.10: And he brought before Him all these. And be divided them equally, and set the divisions a division against his fellow; but the birds he did not divide.
15.11: And the fowl descended upon the divisions, and Abram drave them away.
15.12: And it was sunset, and sleep fell upon Abram: and, lo, a horror of great darkness fell upon him.
15.13: And He said unto Abram, Knowing thou shalt know that thy sons will be sojourners (or aliens) in a land not theirs, and they will serve among them; and they will afflict them four hundred years.
15.14: And the people whom they will serve I will judge, and go forth with much substance.
15.15: And thou shalt be gathered to thy fathers in peace, and shalt be buried in good old age.
15.16: And in the fourth age (or generation) they will return hither; because not (yet) complete is the guilt of the Amoraah.
15.17: And it was at the going away of the sun, and there was darkness. And behold a furnace that burned, and a flame of fire which passed between those divisions.
15.18: In that day the Lord compacted with Abram a covenant, saying, To thy sons will I give this land; from the river of Mizraim unto the great river, the river of Pherat, the Shalmaee,
15.19: and the Kenizaee, and the Kadmonaee,
15.20: and the Hittaee, and the Pherizaee, and the Gibbaraee,
15.21: and the Amoraee, and the Kenaanaee, and the Girgashaee, and the Yebusaee.

16.1: And Sara wife of Abram had no child; and she had an handmaid, a Mizretha, and her name was Hagar.
16.2: And Sara said to Abram, Behold now, the Lord hath restrained me from childbearing; go in now to my handmaid, if, perhaps, I may have sons from her. And Abram received the word of Sara.
16.3: And Sara wife of Abram took Hagar her handmaid, the Mizretha, at the end of ten years of Abram’s dwelling in the land of Kenaan, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife;
16.4: And he went in unto Hagar, and she conceived, and she saw that she had conceived, and her mistress was despised in her eyes.
16.5: And Sara said to Abram, I have (a cause of) judgment against thee. I have given my handmaid to thee, and she seeth that she hath conceived, and I am despised in her eyes: the Lord judge between me and thee.
16.6: And Abram said to Sara, Behold, thy handmaid is in thy hand, do to her as is pleasing in thine eyes: and Sara afflicted her, and she fled from before her.
16.7: And the Angel of the Lord found her at the fountain of water in the wilderness, at the fountain in the way of Hagra.
16.8: And he said, Hagar handmaid of Sara, whence comest thou, and whither art thou going? And she said, From before Sara my mistress do I escape.
16.9: And the Angel of the Lord said to her, Return to thy mistress and be subject under her hand.
16.10: And the Angel of the Lord said to her: Multiplying I will multiply thy sons, and they shall not be numbered for multitude.
16.11: And the Angel of the Lord said to her, Behold, thou hast conceived, and shalt give birth to a son, and thou shalt call his name Yishmael, because the Lord hath heard thy prayer.
16.12: And he will be untameable by man, and he will be needy to everyone, and also all men will be needy to him, and before the face of all his brethren will he dwell.
16.13: And she prayed in the Name of the Lord who had spoken with her; and she said: Thou art Eloha, seeing all: for she said, I also have begun to see after that He hath been revealed to me.
16.14: Therefore she called the name of the well, The well at which appeared the Angel of the Covenant: behold, it is between Rekam and Hagra.
16.15: And Hagar bare to Abram a son, and Abram called the name of his son whom Hagar bare Yishmael.
16.16: And Abram was son of eighty and six years when Hagar bare Yishmael unto Abram.

17.1: And Abram was son of ninety and nine years: and the Lord was revealed to Abram, and said to him, I am EI-shadai; serve before Me, and be perfect;
17.2: And I will set a covenant between My Word and thee, and I will multiply thee exceedingly much.
17.3: And Abram fell on his face: and the Lord spake with him, saying,
17.4: Behold, I have dedicated My covenant with thee, and thou shalt be the father of many peoples,
17.5: and thy name shall no more be called Abram; but thy name shall be Abraham, because the father of many peoples have I appointed (given) thee.
17.6: And I will spread thee abroad very greatly, and I will appoint to thee that assemblies and kings who shall rule the peoples, from thee shall come forth.
17.7: And I will establish My covenant between My Word and thee, and thy sons after thee unto perpetual generations, to be unto thee a God, and to thy sons after thee.
17.8: And I will give to thee and to thy sons after thee the land of thy habitation, all the land of Kenaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be unto them Eloha.
17.9: And the Lord said to Abraham, And thou My covenant shalt keep, thou and thy sons after thee in their generations.
17.10: This is My covenant which you shall keep between My Word and you and thy sons after thee, to circumcise every male that is among you.
17.11: And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be for the sign of the covenant between My Word and you.
17.12: And the son of eight days shall be circumcised among you; every male in your generations, born in the house, or bought with money, of every son of the peoples, who is not of thy sons, circumcising you shall circumcise
17.13: the one born in the house, and him bought with money; and it shall be My covenant in your flesh for a covenant forever.
17.14: And the male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that man shall perish from the people (because) he hath made void My covenant.
17.15: And the Lord said to Abraham, The name of Sara thy wife shall not be called Sara, for Sarah shall be her name:
17.16: And I will bless her, and I will also give thee a son from her; and I will bless her, and assemblies and kings which have dominion over peoples from her shall be.
17.17: And Abraham fell upon his face and rejoiced, and said in his heart, Will the son of a hundred years have a child, and Sarah the daughter of ninety years bring forth?
17.18: And Abraham said before the Lord, O that Yishmael may be established before thee!
17.19: And the Lord said, In verity Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name Izhak; and I will establish My covenant with him for an everlasting covenant to his sons after him.
17.20: And concerning Yishmael I have accepted thy prayer. Behold, I have blessed him, and I will spread him abroad very greatly. Twelve princes will he beget, and I will set him (as) a great people.
17.21: But My covenant I will establish with Izhak, whom Sarah shall bear to thee, at this time, in the year following.
17.22: And when He had ended to speak with him, the Glory of the Lord ascended up from Abraham.
17.23: And Abraham took Yishmael his son, and everyone born in his house, and everyone bought with his money, every male, the men of the house of Abraham, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in that very same day when the Lord had spoken with him.
17.24: And Abraham was son of ninety and nine years, when he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin.
17.25: And Yishmael his son was son of thirteen years, when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
17.26: In that same day Abraham was circumcised, and Yishmael his son,
17.27: And all the men of his house, (whether) born in his house, or bought with money from the sons of the Gentiles, were circumcised with him.

18.1: And the Lord was revealed to him in the Vale of Mamre; and he sat in the door of the tent while the day was hot.
18.2: And lie lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, three men stood towards him; and he saw, and ran from the door of the tent to meet them, and worshipped upon the earth.
18.3: And he said, Lord, if now I have found favour in Thine eyes, pass not, I pray, from Thy servant.
18.4: Accept now a little water, and wash your feet, and recline under the tree,
18.5: and take a mouthful of bread, and strengthen your hearts, afterward you shall pass on; because for this you have come over unto your servant. And He said, So do as thou hast spoken.
18.6: And Abraham hastened to the tent to Sarah, and said, Make haste with three seyin of the flour of meal, mix and make cakes.
18.7: And to the herd ran Abraham, and took a calf, tender and good, and gave to a young man, and he hastened to dress him.
18.8: And he took butter and milk, and the calf which he had prepared, and set before them, and he waited upon them under the tree, and they ate.
18.9: And He said to him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent.
18.10: And He said, Returning I will return to thee, according to the time that you shall revive, and, behold, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard in the door of the tent, and it was behind Him.
18.11: And Abraham and Sarah were old and advanced in days, and with Sarah had ceased to be the way of women.
18.12: And Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After that I am old shall I have a child, and my lord (being also) old?
18.13: And the Lord said to Abraham, Wherefore laughed Sarah, saying, Can it be in truth that I shall bring forth, and I being old?
18.14: What word is hidden from before the Lord? At the time I will return to thee, according to the time that you shall revive, and Sarah shall have a son.
18.15: And Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not: for she was afraid. And He said, No, but thou didst laugh.
18.16: And the men arose thence, and looked towards the face of Sedom; and Abraham went with them to accompany them.
18.17: And the Lord said, Shall I conceal from Abraham what I am doing?
18.18: And Abraham shall be indeed a people many and strong, and in him shall all the peoples of the earth be blessed;
18.19: because it is manifest before me that he will instruct his children, and the men of his house after him, to keep the ways which are right before the Lord, to do righteousness and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which He hath spoken concerning him.
18.20: And the Lord said, The cry of Sedom and Amorah (is heard before Me) because it is great, and the guilt of them is very mighty:
18.21: I will now see, and will judge, whether they do according to the report of them which hath ascended before me. I will deal with them thoroughly unless they convert; but if they convert, I will not punish.
18.22: And the men turned away from thence, and went toward Sedom.
18.23: And Abraham yet ministered in prayer before the Lord. And Abraham approached, and said, Wilt Thou, in anger, destroy the righteous with the guilty?
18.24: If perhaps there be fifty righteous within the city, wilt Thou in anger destroy and not forgive the place for the fifty righteous who are within it?
18.25: More true are Thy judgments than that Thou shouldst do a thing like that, to destroy the just with the guilty, and that the just should be as the guilty! Thy judgments are true! Can the Judge of all the earth but do justice?
18.26: And the Lord said, If I find in Sedom fifty righteous in the midst of the city, I will spare all the place for their sake.
18.27: And Abraham answered and said, Behold, I have done a great thing, to speak before the Lord, and I dust and ashes!
18.28: Perhaps of the fifty righteous there may be wanting five: shall all the city perish through five? And He said, I will not destroy, if I find there forty and five.
18.29: And he added yet to speak before Him, and said, Perhaps forty may be found there. And He said, I will not make the end on account of the forty.
18.30: And he said, Let not the anger of the Lord now kindle, and I will speak. Perhaps thirty shall be found there. And He said, I will not make the end if I find there thirty.
18.31: And he said, Behold, I have done a great thing to speak before the Lord: perhaps twenty shall be found there. And He said, I will not destroy for the sake of twenty.
18.32: And he said, Let not now the anger of the Lord kindle, and I will speak only this time: perhaps ten may be found there. And He said, I will not destroy for the sake of the ten!
18.33: And the Glory of the Lord ascended when He had ceased to speak with Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.

19.1: And two angels entered into Sedom in the evening; and Lot sat in the gate of Sedom. And Lot saw, and arose to present himself before them, and he bowed with his face to the earth.
19.2: And he said, I pray my lords (ribboni) to turn aside unto the house of your servant and lodge, and wash your feet; and rising early you shall go on your way. And they said, Not so, but in the wide place will we lodge.
19.3: And he was greatly in earnest with them, and they turned aside with him, and entered into his house: and he made them a supper, and dressed unleavened cakes for them, and they ate.
19.4: As yet they had not slept; and the men of the city, the men of Sedom, gathered against the house, from the youth unto the old man, all the people from the extremes;
19.5: And they cried to Lot, and said to him, Where are the men who came to thee tonight? Bring them forth to us, and we will know them.
19.6: And Lot went out to them to the gate, and the door he shut after him.
19.7: And he said, I pray you, my brethren, do not (so) wickedly.
19.8: Behold, now, I have two daughters, who have not known man, I would bring them to you, and you should do to them what pleases in your eyes; only to these men do nothing, because they have entered under the shadow of my dwelling.
19.9: And they said, Go in, however! And they said, One came to sojourn, and, behold, he judgeth judgment! Now will we do worse to thee than to them; and they prevailed against the man, against Lot, greatly, and came nigh to shatter the door.
19.10: And the men put forth their hands, and brought in Lot to be with them in the house, and shut the door.
19.11: And the men who were at the gate of the house they smote with blindness, from the little to the great, and they were wearied to find the gate.
19.12: And the men said to Lot, Whomsoever thou hast yet here, thy son-in-law, and thy sons, and thy daughters, and all that thou hast in the city, lead out from the place:
19.13: For we will destroy this place, because their cry is great before the Lord, and the Lord hath sent us to destroy it.
19.14: And Lot went forth, and spake with his sons-in-law, the takers of his daughters, and said, Arise, come forth from this place; for the Lord will destroy the city. And he was as a trifler in the eyes of his sons-in-law.
19.15: And it was as the morning rose that the angels were urgent upon Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife and thy two daughters who are found faithful with thee, lest thou be smitten with the punishment of the city.
19.16: But he delayed; and the men laid hold of his hands, and of the hand of his wife, and of the hand of his two daughters; for the Lord had mercy upon him; and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.
19.17: And it was when he had brought them without, he said, Be merciful on thy life, look not behind thee, and stand not in all the plain, escape to the mountain for deliverance, lest thou perish.
19.18: And Lot said to them, Be entreated, O Lord;
19.19: behold now, Thy servant hath found mercy before Thee, and Thou hast magnified Thy goodness which Thou hast shown me in saving my life, and I cannot take refuge in the mountain, lest evil befall me, and I die.
19.20: Behold now, this city is nigh, to flee there; and it is (but) small; let me now escape thither. Is it not small? And my life shall be sustained.
19.21: And He said to him, Behold, I have accepted thee in this thing also, in that I will not overthrow the city for which thou hast prayed.
19.22: Haste, escape thither; for I cannot do anything until thou be come thither. Therefore be called the name of the city Zoar.
19.23: The sun had come forth upon the earth, and Lot entered Zoar.
19.24: And the Lord rained upon Sedom and upon Amorah sulphur and fire from before the Lord from the heavens,
19.25: and destroyed those cities and all the plain, and all the dwellers in the cities and the herbage of the earth.
19.26: And his wife looked behind her, and she became a statue of salt.
19.27: And Abraham ascended in the morning to the place where he had ministered in prayer before the Lord;
19.28: And he looked toward Sedom and Amorah, and upon all the place of the plain land, and saw, and, behold, the smoke of the land went up as the smoke of a furnace.
19.29: And it was when the Lord destroyed the cities of the plain, that the Lord remembered Abraham, and sent Lot from the midst of the overthrow, when He overthrew the cities in which Lot dwelt.
19.30: And Lot went up from Zoar, and dwelt in the mountain, and his two daughters with him: for he feared to dwell in Zoar; and he dwelt in a cavern, he and his two daughters.
19.31: And the elder said to the younger, Our father is aged, and there is no man in the earth to go in unto us according to the way of all the earth.
19.32: Come, we will pour father wine, and will lie with him, and raise up sons from our father.
19.33: And they poured their father wine in that night; and the elder went in and lay with her father; and he knew not, in her lying down nor in her rising up.
19.34: And it was in the day which followed that the elder said to the younger, Behold, I lay yesterday with the father: let us give wine also in the night, and go thou in, lie with him, and we will raise up sons from our father.
19.35: And they gave that night also wine to their father, and the younger arose and lay with him; and he knew not, in her lying down nor in her rising up.
19.36: And the two daughters of Lot conceived from their father;
19.37: And the elder brought forth a son, and called his name Moab: he is the father of the Moabaee unto this day.
19.38: And the younger also brought forth a son, and she called his name Bar Ammi: he is the father of the B’ni Ammon unto this day.

20.1: And Abraham migrated from thence to the southern land, and dwelt between Rekam and Hagra; and he sojourned in Gerar.
20.2: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, She is my sister. And Abimelek, king of Gerar, sent and took Sarah.
20.3: And the word came from the presence of the Lord to Abimelek in a dream of the night, and said to him, Behold, thou diest, on account of the woman whom thou hast taken, and she a man’s wife.
20.4: But Abimelek had not come nigh her. And he said, Lord, wilt Thou also kill the innocent people?
20.5: Did he not say to me, She is my sister? And she also said, He is my brother. In the rectitude of my heart, and the cleanness of my bands, have I done this.
20.6: And the Lord said to him in a dream, It is also manifest to Me that in the integrity of thy heart thou hast done this, and I have also restrained thee from sinning before Me; therefore I have not permitted thee to approach to her.
20.7: And now return the mares wife; for he is a prophet, and he will pray for thee, and thou shalt live. But if thou wilt not return (her), know that dying thou shalt die, thou, and all who are thine.
20.8: And Abimelek arose in the morning, and called all his servants, and spake all these words before them; and the men feared greatly.
20.9: And Abimelek called Abraham, and said to him, What hast thou done to us, and in what have I sinned against thee, that thou shouldst have brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? Works which are not worthy to be done hast thou done with me.
20.10: And Abimelek said to Abraham, What sawest thou, that thou didst this thing?
20.11: And Abraham spake, Because I said, Perhaps the fear of the Lord is not in this place, and they will kill me on account of my wife.
20.12: Nevertheless, in truth she is my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.
20.13: And it was, when the people erred after the works of their hands, the Lord did bring me near to the fear of Himself, from (among) the house of my father. And I said to her, This is thy favour which thou canst do for me; in every place through which we pass, say of me, He is my brother.
20.14: And Abimelek took sheep, and oxen, and servants, and handmaidens, and gave to Abraham, and returned to him Sarah his wife.
20.15: And Abimelek said, Behold, my land is before thee: where it is pleasant in thine eyes, dwell.
20.16: And to Sarah he said, Behold, I have given a thousand seleen of silver to thy brother; behold, that is to thee a veil of honour, for my having sent to take thee, and to see thee, and all that is with thee; and concerning all whatever thou hast spoken thou art reproved.
20.17: And Abraham prayed before the Lord, and the Lord healed Abimelek, and his wife, and his handmaids, and they were revived:
20.18: For the Lord had shut all the wombs of the house of Abimelek, on account of Sarah, the wife of Abraham.

21.1: And the Lord remembered Sarah as He had said; and the Lord did unto Sarah according as He had spoken.
21.2: And Sarah conceived and bare unto Abraham a son in his old age, in the time of which the Lord had told him.
21.3: And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bare to him, Izhak.
21.4: And Abraham circumcised Izhak his son (when) the son of eight days, as the Lord had commanded him.
21.5: And Abraham was the son of a hundred years when Izhak his son was born to him.
21.6: And Sarah said, The Lord hath made me to have gladness; everyone who heareth will give me joy.
21.7: And she said, Faithful is He who spake unto Abraham, and certified that Sarah should suckle children; for she hath born a son in his old age.
21.8: And the child grew, and was weaned; and Abraham made a great feast in the day when Izhak was weaned.
21.9: And Sarah observed the son of Hagar the Mizritha, whom she bare to Abraham, deriding.
21.10: And she said, Cast out this handmaid and her son; for the son of the handmaid shall not inherit with my son, with Izhak.
21.11: And the word was evil exceedingly in the eyes of Abraham, on account of his son.
21.12: And the Lord said to Abraham, Let it not be evil in thine eyes concerning the youth and concerning thine handmaid. All that Sarah saith to thee receive from her, because in Izhak shall thy sons be called to thee.
21.13: And also the son of the handmaid will I set for a people, because he is thy son.
21.14: And Abraham rose up in the morning, and took bread and a skin of water, and gave to Hagar, setting upon her shoulder, and the youth, and dismissed her. And she went, and wandered in the desert of the well of Shava (Beara de Shava).
21.15: And the water was finished from the skin; and she laid the youth under one of the trees,
21.16: And (she) went and sat over against, as far off as a bow flight: for she said, I cannot see the death of the child. And she sat over against, and lifted up her voice and wept.
21.17: And the voice of the youth was heard before the Lord; and the Angel of the Lord called to Hagar from the heavens, and said to her, What to thee, Hagar? Fear not, for the voice of the youth is heard before the Lord in the place where he is.
21.18: Arise, take up the youth and strengthen thine hand in him, because for a great people have I appointed him.
21.19: And the Lord opened her eyes, and she saw the well of waters, and went and filled the skin with water, and gave the youth to drink.
21.20: And the Word of the Lord was the Helper of the youth, and he grew and dwelt in the wilderness, and became a master of the bow.
21.21: And he dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took for him a wife from the land of Mizraim.
21.22: And it was in that time that Abimelek and Phikol, chief of his host, spake to Abraham, saying, The Word of the Lord is thy Helper in everything thou doest;
21.23: And now swear to me here, by the Word of the Lord, that thou wilt not be false with me, nor with my son, nor with my son’s son; and that according to the good which I have done to thee thou wilt do with me and with the land in which thou art a sojourner.
21.24: And Abraham said, I will swear.
21.25: And Abraham reproved Abimelek, on account of the well of waters which the servants of Abimelek had taken by force.
21.26: And Abimelek said, I knew not if this thing had been done, and thou also hadst not shown me, nor have I heard, but this day.
21.27: And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave to Abimelek, and they struck both of them a covenant.
21.28: And Abraham made seven lambs stand apart; and
21.29: Abimelek said to Abraham, What are these seven lambs which thou hast made to stand apart?
21.30: And he said, That thou mayest take the seven lambs seven lambs from my hand, to testify for me that I have digged that well.
21.31: Therefore he called that place Beer Shava, because there they sware together.
21.32: And they struck a covenant at Beer Shava. And Abimelek and Phikol, the chief of his host, arose, and returned to the land of the Phelishtaee.
21.33: And he planted a tree in Beer Shava, and prayed there in the name of the Lord, the Most High God.
21.34: And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Phelislitaee many days.

22.1: And it was after these things that the Lord tempted Abraham; and He said to him, Abraham! And he said, Behold, I am.
22.2: And He said, Take now thy son, thy only, whom thou lovest, Izhak, and go into the land of worship, and offer him before Me there, a burnt offering, upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee.
22.3: And Abraham arose in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Izhak his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering, and arose and went to the place of which the Lord had spoken to him.
22.4: And in the third day Abraham lifted, up his eyes, and saw the place from afar.
22.5: And Abraham said to his young men, Wait you here with the ass, and I and the young man will ascend yonder and worship, and return to you.
22.6: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering, and laid on Izhak his son; and he took in his hand the fire and the knife, and they went both of them as one.
22.7: And Izhak spake to Abraham his father, and said, Father! And he said, Behold, I am, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood; but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?
22.8: And Abraham said, The lamb for the burnt offering is revealed before the Lord, my son. And they went, both of them, as one.
22.9: And they came to the place of which the Lord had told him. And Abraham builded there the altar, and set in order the woods, and bound Izhak his son, and laid him upon the altar above the woods.
22.10: And Abraham stretched forth his hand and took the knife to cut off his son.
22.11: And the Angel of the Lord called to him from the heavens, and said, Abraham, Abraham! And he said, Behold, I am.
22.12: And he said to him, Stretch not out thy hand upon the youth, neither do anything to him: for now I know that thou fearest the Lord, and that thou hast not spared thy only son for Me.
22.13: And Abraham lifted up his eyes after these (words), and saw, and behold, one ram, holden in the bush by his horns. And Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him for a burnt offering instead of his son.
22.14: And Abraham worshipped and prayed there in that place, and said before the Lord, Here shall generations worship: wherefore it shall be paid in that day, In this mountain Abraham worshipped before the Lord.
22.15: And the Angel of the Lord called to Abraham the second time from the heavens,
22.16: And said, By my Word have I sworn, saith the Lord, because thou hast done this thing, and hast not spared thy only son,
22.17: therefore, blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thy sons as the stars of heaven and as the sand which is on the sea shore; and thy sons shall inherit the cities of their enemies.
22.18: And all the peoples of the earth shall be blessed through thy son: forasmuch as thou hast received My word.
22.19: And Abraham returned to his young men, and they arose and went together unto Beer Shava, and Abraham dwelt in Beer Shava.
22.20: And it was after these things it was shown to Abraham, saying, Behold, Milcha, also, hath born sons to Nachor, thy brother:
22.21: Uts his first-born, and Booz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
22.22: and Kesed, and Chazu, and Phildash, and Yedlaph, and Bethuel.
22.23: And Bethuel begat Revekah. These eight bare Milcha to Nahor, brother of Abraham.
22.24: And his concubine, whose name was Reuma, she also bare Tebach, and Gacham, and Tachash, and Maaka.

23.1: And the life of Sarah was a hundred and twenty and seven years, the years of the life of Sarah.
23.2: And Sarah died in Kiryath-arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Kenaan. And Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to lament her.
23.3: And Abraham rose up from the presence of his dead, and spake with the sons of Hittah, saying,
23.4: I am a guest and a sojourner with you: give me the possession of a sepulchre with you, that I may bury my dead from before me.
23.5: And the sons of Hittah answered Abraham, saying to him,
23.6: Receive from us Ribbona; a prince before the Lord art thou among us; in the best of our sepulchres bury thy dead. No man of us will refuse his sepulchre to thee for the burial of thy dead.
23.7: And Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land, the sons of Hittah.
23.8: And he spake with them, saying, If you are willing in your minds that I should bury my dead from before me, receive from me, and request for me of Ephron bar Zochar
23.9: That he will give me the Double Cavern, which is in the side of his field: for the full amount (shelim) of silver he shall give it to me among you for the possession of a sepulchre.
23.10: But Ephron was sitting in the midst of the sons of Hittah; and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham before the sons of Hittah, of all entering the gate of the city, saying,
23.11: No, my lord; receive of me; I will present to thee the field and the cavern which is in it; to thee will I present it; in sight of the sons of my people will I present it to thee. Bury thy dead.
23.12: And Abraham bowed before the people of the land.
23.13: And he spake with Ephron before the people of the land, saying, Nevertheless, if thou wilt do me a grace, receive from me; I will give money for the field; take of me, and I will bury my dead there.
23.14: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,
23.15: My lord, receive of me: the land is worth four hundred sileen of silver; between me and thee what is it? Bury thy dead.
23.16: And Abraham agreed with Ephron, and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver of which be had spoken before the sons of Hittah, four hundred sileen of silver, which is received in merchandise in every city.
23.17: And Ephron confirmed the field in which is the double cavern which is before Mamre; the field, and the cavern that is therein, and all the trees which were in the field, in all its boundaries round about,
23.18: To Abraham, for a purchase, in the sight of the sons of Hitah, of all entering the gate of the city.
23.19: And after this Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the double cavern of the field which is before Mamre, that is Hebron, in the land of Kenaan.
