23.20: And the field and the cavern which is in it were confirmed to Abraham for the possession of a sepulchre from the sons of Hittah.

24.1: And Abraham was old, (and) advanced in days, and the Lord had blessed Abraham in all things.
24.2: And Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who had authority over all which was his, Put now thy hand under my thigh,
24.3: And I will adjure thee by the Word of the Lord, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that thou wilt not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Kenaanaee among whom I dwell.
24.4: But to my country and to my kindred thou wilt go, and take a wife for my son Izhak.
24.5: And the servant said to him, Perhaps the woman will not be willing to come after me to this land, returning am I to return thy son to the land from which thou hast gone forth?
24.6: And Abraham said to him, Take care that thou return not my son thither;
24.7: The Lord, the God of heaven, who took me from the house of my father and from the land of my birth, and who spake to me, and sware to me, saying, I will give thee this land, will send His angel before thee, and thou wilt take a wife for my son from thence.
24.8: And if the woman be not willing to come after thee, thou shalt be absolved from this my oath; only cause not my son to return thither.
24.9: And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sware to him concerning that matter.
24.10: And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his lord and went. And all the goods of his master were in his hand. And he arose and went to Aram, which is upon Phrath, the river, to the city of Nachor.
24.11: And he made the camels rest without the city at a well of waters in the evening time, at the time when they came forth to fill.
24.12: And he said, Lord God of my master Abraham, let it, I pray, be opportune with me this day, and deal thou graciously with my master Abraham.
24.13: Behold, I stand by the fountain of waters, and the daughters of the men of the city will come forth to draw water.
24.14: Let the maiden to whom I shall say, Reach thy waterpot, I pray, that I may drink; and she say, Drink, and I will also give thy camels drink, be she whom Thou hast prepared for Thy servant, for Izhak: and in this I shall know that Thou hast dealt graciously with my master.
24.15: And it was while he had not ceased to speak that, behold, Revekah came forth, (she) who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcha, wife of Nachor, brother of Abraham, and her pitcher upon her shoulder.
24.16: And the maiden was very fair to behold; a virgin, and man had not known her; and she descended to the fountain, and filled her pitcher, and came up.
24.17: And the servant hasted to her presence; and said, Let me taste, I pray, a little water from thy pitcher.
24.18: And she said, Drink, Ribboni; and she made haste, and held her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him to drink.
24.19: And when she had ended giving him drink, she said, For thy camels also I will draw, until they shall have enough to drink.
24.20: And she hastened and poured out her pitcher into the place of watering, and ran again to the well to fill, and she filled for all his camels.
24.21: And the man wondered at her, gazing silently, to know whether the Lord had prospered his way or not.
24.22: And it was when the camels had drunk enough, the man took a ring (qadasha) of gold weighing a shekel, and two bracelets (sherin) for the hand weighing ten sileen of gold.
24.23: And he said, Whose daughter art thou? Tell me, I pray, whether there be room in thy father’s house sufficient for us to lodge?
24.24: And she said to him, I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcha, whom she bare to Nachor.
24.25: And she said to him, There is much straw and provender with us, also room enough to lodge.
24.26: And the man kneeled, and worshipped before the Lord,
24.27: and said, Blessed be the Lord the God of my master Abraham, who hath not withheld His grace and His truth from my master; and me hath the Lord led in a right way to the house of my master’s brother.
24.28: And the maiden ran and showed these things to her mother’s house.
24.29: And Revekah had a brother whose name was Laban; and Laban ran to the man without at the fountain.
24.30: And it was when he saw the ring and the bracelets upon the hands of his sister, and heard the words of Revekah his sister, saying, As this spake the man with me, that he came to the man, and, behold, he stood by the camels at the fountain;
24.31: And he said, Enter, blessed of the Lord; why standest thou without? And I have a prepared house and a proper place for the camels.
24.32: And the man entered the house, and he loosed the camels, and gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men who were with him.
24.33: And they set before him to eat. And he said, I will not eat until I have spoken my words. And he said, Speak.
24.34: And he said, I am a servant of Abraham;
24.35: And the Lord hath blessed my master much, and increased, and hath given to him sheep and oxen, silver and gold, servants and handmaidens, camels and asses.
24.36: And Sarah the wife of my master bare a son to my master after she was old, and he hath given to him all that he hath.
24.37: And my master adjured me, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife for my son from the daughters of Kenaan in whose land I dwell;
24.38: But thou shalt go to my father’s house, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son.
24.39: And I said to my master, Perhaps the woman will not come after me.
24.40: And he said to me, The Lord before whom I worship will send His angel with thee, and will prosper thy way, and thou shalt take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father’s house.
24.41: Then shalt thou be absolved from my oath when thou hast gone to my kindred: and if they will not give unto thee, thou shalt be absolved from my oath.
24.42: And I came this day to the fountain, and I said, Lord God of my master Abraham, if now it is pleasing before thee to prosper the way in which I go,
24.43: Behold, I stand at the fountain of waters, and a damsel may come forth to fill; and I will say to her, Give me to drink, I entreat, a little water from thy pitcher;
24.44: And she shall say to me, Both for thee and thy camels also I will fill, let her be the wife whom the Lord hath ordained for my master’s son.
24.45: And I had not left speaking in my heart, when, behold, Revekah came forth, with her pitcher upon her shoulder, and went down to the fountain and filled. And I said to her, Let me now drink.
24.46: And she hastened and let down her pitcher, and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels also drink. And I drank, and the camels also she watered.
24.47: And I asked her and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she said, I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nachor, whom Milcha bare to him. And I set an ornament on her face, and bracelets upon her hand,
24.48: and bowed down and worshipped before the Lord, and blessed the Lord God of my master Abraham who had led me in a true way, to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
24.49: And now, if you will act with goodness and truth with my master, show me; and if not, I will turn to the right or to the left.
24.50: And Laban answered, and Bethuel, and said, From before the Lord the word hath come forth: we have no power to say to thee either evil or good.
24.51: Behold, Revekah is before thee; take (her) and go; and let her be the wife of thy master’s son, as the Lord hath spoken.
24.52: And it was, when the servant of Abraham heard these words, he worshipped on the earth before the Lord.
24.53: And the servant brought out vessels of silver and vessels of gold and vestments, and gave to Revekah, and presents gave he to her brother and to her mother.
24.54: And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and they lodged and arose in the morning. And he said, Send me to my master.
24.55: And her brother said, and her mother, Let the maiden abide with us a season of time, or ten months; after that she shall go.
24.56: And he said to them, Keep me not back: the Lord will direct my way, and I will proceed to my master.
24.57: And they said, We will call the maiden, and hear what she will say.
24.58: And they called Revekah, and said to her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.
24.59: And they dismissed Revekah their sister, and her nurse, and the servant of Abraham, and his men.
24.60: And they blessed Revekah, and said to her, Thou art our sister; be thou (multiplied) unto thousands and myriads, and may thy children inherit the cities of those who hate them.
24.61: And Revekah arose, and her maidens; and they rode upon camels, and went after the man. And the servant took Revekah and went.
24.62: And Izhak ascended in coming from the well over which the Angel of Life (malak qayama, “the Eternal Angel”) had appeared; and he dwelt in the land of the south.
24.63: And Izhak went forth to pray in the field, at the presence of the evening; and he lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, the camels came.
24.64: And Revekah lifted up her eyes, and saw Izhak; and she bowed herself on the camel.
24.65: And she said to the servant, Who is the man who is walking in the field to meet us? And the servant said, He is my master. And she took a mantle and covered herself.
24.66: And the servant recounted to Izhak all the things which he had done.
24.67: And Izhak brought her to the tabernacle: and he saw, and, behold, her works were right as the works of Sarah his mother. And he took Revekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. And Izhak was comforted after his mother.

25.1: And Abraham added, and took a wife, and her name was Keturah;
25.2: And she bare to him Zimran, and Yokshan, and Medan, and Midyan, and Yeshbach, and Shuvach.
25.3: And Yokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan; and the sons of Dedan have been in camps and tabernacles and islands.
25.4: And the sons of Midyan, Eipha, and Epher, and Hanok, and Abidah, and Eldaah: all these the sons of Keturah.
25.5: And Abraham gave all that he had unto Izhak.
25.6: But to the sons of the concubine of Abraham gave Abraham portions, and sent them from his son Izhak, while he yet lived, eastward in the land of the sunrise.
25.7: And these are the days of the years of the life of Abraham that he lived, an hundred and seventy and five years.
25.8: And Abraham expired, and died in a good old age, aged, and full of days; and he was gathered unto his people.
25.9: And Izhak and Ishmael his sons buried him in the twofold cave in the field of Ephron bar Zochar, the Hittah, which is before Mamre;
25.10: the field that Abraham bought from the sons of Hittah: there they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife.
25.11: And it was after the death of Abraham that the Lord blessed Izhak his son, and Izhak dwelt at the well over which the Eternal Angel had appeared.
25.12: And these are the generations of Ishmael bar Abraham, whom Hagar the Mizretha, the handmaid of Sarah, bare to Abraham.
25.13: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael by their names in their generations. The firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; and Kedar, and Adbeel,
25.14: and Mibsam, and Mishma, and Duma, and Massa;
25.15: Hadad, and Thema, Yetoor, Naphish, and Kedemah.
25.16: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names in their villages and their towns, twelve chiefs of their peoples.
25.17: And these are the years of the life of Ishmael, a hundred and thirty and seven years. And he expired and died, and was gathered to his people.
25.18: And they have dwelt from Havilah unto Hagra, which looketh toward Mizraim, reaching unto Athoor. In the presence of all his brethren he dwelt.
25.19: And these are the generations of Izhak bar Abraham. Abraham begat Izhak;
25.20: And Izhak was a son of forty years when he took Revekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramite of Padan Aram, the sister of Laban the Aramite, to be his wife.
25.21: And Izhak prayed before the Lord for his wife, because she was barren; and the Lord hearkened to his prayer, and Revekah his wife conceived.
25.22: And the children struggled in her womb; and she said, If thus, why have I conceived? And she went to seek instruction before the Lord:
25.23: And the Lord said to her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two kingdoms from thy womb shall be divided, and (one) kingdom (shall be) stronger than (the other) kingdom, and the greater shall be subject to the less.
25.24: And her days were fulfilled to give birth. And, behold, twins were in her womb.
25.25: And the first came forth red, all of him as a garment (covering) of hair; and they called his name Esau.
25.26: And afterwards came forth his brother, and his hand grasped the heel of Esau, and they called his name Jakob. And Izhak was sixty years old when he begat them.
25.27: And the youths grew; and Esau was a man of idleness, a man going out into the field; and Jakob was a man of peace, a minister of the house of instruction.
25.28: And Izhak loved Esau, because he ate of his hunting, and Rivekah loved Jakob.
25.29: And Jakob dressed pottage, and Esau came from the field, and he was faint.
25.30: And Esau said to Jakob, Let me taste now of that red, that red! For I am faint: (therefore he called his name Edom:)
25.31: and Jakob said, Sell this day thy birthright to me.
25.32: And Esau said, Behold, I am going to die, and what is this birthright to me?
25.33: And Jakob said, Swear to me today; and he sware to him and he sold his birthright to Jakob.
25.34: And Jakob gave to Esau bread and pottage of lentiles. And he ate and drank, and arose, and went: and Esau despised the birthright.

26.1: And there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine that was in the days of Abraham; and Izhak went to Abimelek, king of the Philistaee, to Gerar.
26.2: And the Lord appeared to him and said, Go not down into Mizraim, remain in the land as I have told thee;
26.3: Dwell in this land, and My Word shall be to thee for a helper; and I will bless thee. For to thee and to thy son will I give all these lands; and I will confirm the oath that I have sworn to Abraham thy father;
26.4: And I will multiply thy son as the stars of heaven, and will give thy son all these lands, and through thy son shall all the peoples of the earth be blessed,
26.5: because Abraham obeyed My word, and kept the keeping of My word, My commandments, My covenant, and My law.
26.7: and the men of the place asked respecting his wife. And he said, She is my sister; for he feared to say, My wife, lest the men of the place should kill him on account of Revekah; for she was of beautiful aspect.
26.8: And it was when be had been there many days that Abimelek the king of the Philistaee looked from a window, and, behold, Izhak was sporting with Revekah his wife.
26.9: And Abimelek called Izhak and said, Nevertheless, behold, she is thy wife: why then hast thou said, She is my sister? And Izhak said to him, Because I said, Lest I be killed on account of her.
26.10: And Abimelek said, What is this that thou hast done to us? It might have been that some one of the people had lain with thy wife, and thou wouldst have brought upon us the guilt.
26.11: And Abimelek commanded all the people saying, Whoever injureth this man shall surely be put to death.
26.12: And Izhak sowed in the land, and found in that year a hundred fold on that which he had expended, (or estimated,) and the Lord blessed him;
26.13: And the man increased, and went on multiplying and increasing, until he had increased greatly.
26.14: And he had flocks of sheep, and herds of cattle, and many servants; and the Philistaee were envious of him.
26.15: And all the wells that the servants of his father had digged in the days of Abraham the Philistaee stopped up, and filled with dust.
26.16: And Abimelek said to Izhak, Go from us; for thou art much stronger than we.
26.17: And Izhak went thence, and sojourned in the vale of Gerar, and dwelt there.
26.18: And Izhak returned, and digged the well of water which they had digged in the days of Abraham his father, and which the Philistaee had stopped after the death of Abraham; and he called their names after the names by which his father had called them.
26.19: And the servants of Izhak digged in the valley, and found there a well of flowing waters.
26.20: And the shepherds of Gerar strove with the shepherds of Izhak, saying, The water is ours; and he called the name of the well Contention, because they had contended with him.
26.21: And they digged another well, and they strove also on account of it, and he called the name of it Hatred.
26.22: And he went up from thence, and digged another well; and for that they strove not: and he called the name of it Spaciousness. For he said, Because now hath the Lord enlarged us, and we shall spread abroad in the land.
26.23: And he went up from thence to Beer Shava;
26.24: and the Lord appeared to him in the night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father; fear not: for in thy help is My Word; and I will bless thee, and will multiply thy sons for the sake of Abraham My servant.
26.25: And he builded there an altar, and prayed in the name of the Lord. And he spread there his tabernacle; and the servants of Izhak digged there a well.
26.26: And Abimelek came to him from Gerar, and a company of his friends, and Phikol the chief of his host.
26.27: And Izhak said to him, Why have you come to me, when you have hated me, and sent me from you?
26.28: And they said, Seeing we have seen that the Word of the Lord is for thy help; and we have said, Let the oath which was between our fathers be now confirmed between us and thee, and let us enter into a covenant with thee,
26.29: that thou do us no evil, as we have not injured thee, and as we have done thee only good, and we will leave thee in peace; thou art now blessed of the Lord.
26.30: And he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
26.31: And they arose in the morning and covenanted, each man with his brother; and Izhak dismissed them, and they went from him in peace.
26.32: And it was in that day that the servants of Izhak came and showed him concerning the well that they had digged. And they said to him, We have found water.
26.33: And he called it Sheva, (the swearing). Wherefore the name of the city is Beer-sheva unto this day.
26.34: And Esau was the son of forty years, and he took to wife Jehudith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite;
26.35: And they were rebels and irritators against the word of Izhak and Revekah.

27.1: And it was, when Izhak was old, and his eyes were darkened from seeing, that he called Esau, his eldest son, and said to him, My son. And he said to him, Behold, I am.
27.2: And he said, Behold now, I am old, I know not the day that I shall die:
27.3: And now take thy weapons, thy knife and thy bow, and go out into the field, and hunt me venison,
27.4: And make me food I such as I like, and bring it to me, and I will eat, and my soul shall bless thee before I die.
27.5: And Revekah listened as Izhak was speaking with his son Esau. And Esau went into the field to hunt venison to bring it.
27.6: And Revekah spake to Jakob, her son, saying, Behold, I have heard thy father speaking with Esau thy brother, saying,
27.7: Bring me now venison, and make me food, and I will eat and bless thee in the presence of the Lord before I die.
27.8: And now, my son, obey me in what I command thee.
27.9: Go now to the flock, and take thee from thence two good goat-kids, and make them into food for thy father such as he loves,
27.10: And carry in to thy father, that he may eat, and bless thee before he die.
27.11: And Jakob said to Revekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
27.12: It may be that my father will feel me, and I shall be in his eyes as a deceiver, and shall bring upon me curses, and not blessings.
27.13: And his mother said to him, Unto me it hath been said in prophecy, that there shall be no curses upon thee, my son; only obey me, and go, and take for me.
27.14: And he went, and took, and brought to his mother, and his mother made food such as his father loved.
27.15: And Revekah took the vestments of Esau her elder son, (which were) clean, and were with her in the house, and clothed Jakob her younger son.
27.16: And with the skins of the kids she covered his hands, and upon the smoothness of his neck.
27.17: And she gave the food and the bread that she had made into the hand of Jakob her son.
27.18: And he went in to his father, and said, Father! And he said, Behold me. Who art thou, my son?
27.19: And Jakob said to his father, I am Esau, thy firstborn: I have done as thou hast told me. Arise now, turn thyself, and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
27.20: And Izhak said to his son, What is this, thou hast so quickly found, my son? And he said, Because the Lord thy God prepared it before me.
27.21: And Izhak said to Jakob, Draw near now, and I will feel thee, my son, whether thou be my son Esau or not.
27.22: And Jakob drew near to Izhak his father, and he felt him, and said, The voice is the voice of Jakob; but the hands are the hands of Esau.
27.23: And he could not be known, because his hands were hairy, like the hands of Esau his brother; and he blessed him.
27.24: And he said, But art thou my son Esau? And he said, I am!
27.25: And he said, Bring before me, and I will eat of my sons venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he offered to him, and he did eat; and he brought him wine, and he drank.
27.26: And Izhak his father said to him, Approach now, and kiss me, my son.
27.27: And he approached, and kissed him, and he smelled the fragrance of his vestments, and blessed him, and said, Lo, the smell of my son is as the fragrance of a field which the Lord hath blessed.
27.28: And the Lord shall give thee of the dew of heaven, and of the goodness of the earth, and abundance of corn and of wine.
27.29: Let the peoples serve thee, and kingdoms be subservient to thee: be thou chief of thy brethren, and let the sons of thy mother worship thee: cursed shall they be who curse thee, and blessed shall they be who bless thee!
27.30: And it was when Izhak had completed to bless Jakob, and Jakob had, going, only gone out from Izhak his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
27.31: And he had also made food, and he brought it to his father, and said to his father, Arise, my father, and eat of thy son’s venison, that thy soul may bless me.
27.32: And Izhak his father said to him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son, thy firstborn, Esau.
27.33: And Izhak was wonderstruck with exceeding great wonder, and said, Who was he who prepared venison, and brought it to me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and I have blessed him? And blessed shall he be.
27.34: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried a cry, great and bitter exceedingly. And he said to his father, Bless me, also, me, father!
27.35: And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath received thy blessing.
27.36: And he said, Rightly is his name called Jakob, he hath dealt subtilly with me these two times; my birthright he took, and, behold, now he hath received my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not left me a blessing?
27.37: And Izhak answered, and said to Esau, Behold, I have set him a chief over thee, and all his brethren I have given to him for servants, and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and for thee now what can I do, my son?
27.38: And Esau said to his father, Hast thou but one blessing, father? Bless me, me also, my father. And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
27.39: And Izhak his father answered and said to him, Behold, thy habitation shall be of the best of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.
27.40: And by thy sword shalt thou live, and thy brother obey; and it will be that when his sons shall have transgressed the words of the law, thou wilt cast his yoke from off thy neck.
27.41: And Esau kept enmity towards Jakob for the blessing wherewith his father had blessed him. And Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for father draw near and I wilt kill Jakob my brother.
27.42: And the words of Esau her eldest son were shown to Revekah, and she sent and called Jakob her younger son, and said to him, Behold, Esau thy brother plotteth against thee to kill thee.
27.43: And now, my son, receive from me, and arise and go to Laban my brother at Haran,
27.44: And dwell with him a few days, until thy brother’s wrath turn away,
27.45: Until the anger of thy brother turn from thee, and what thou hast done to him be forgotten; and I will send and bring thee thence. Why should I be bereaved of both of you in one day?
27.46: And Revekah said to Izhak, I am grieved in my life at the sight of the daughters of Hittah. If Jakob take a wife of the daughters of Hittah, like these of the daughters of the land, what to me is life?

28.1: And Izhak called Jakob and blessed him. And he commanded him, and said to him, Thou shalt not take a wife from the daughters of Kenaan;
28.2: Arise, go to Padan Aram to the house of Bethuel the father of thy mother, and take to thee from thence a wife of the daughters of Laban, the brother of thy mother.
28.3: And the All-sufficient God bless thee, and make thee to increase and multiply, and become an assemblage of tribes;
28.4: And give the blessing of Abraham to thee and thy sons with thee, that thou mayest inherit the land of thy habitation which the Lord gave to Abraham.
28.5: And Izhak sent Jakob away, and he went to Padan Aram to Laban bar Bethuel, the Aramite, the brother of Revekah, the mother of Jakob and Esau.
28.6: And Esau, when he saw that Izhak had blessed Jakob, and sent him to Padan Aram to take from thence a wife, and, as he blessed him, commanded him, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife from the daughters of Kenaan,
28.7: and that Jakob had obeyed his father and his mother, and had gone to Padan Aram,
28.8: Esau, considering that the daughters of Kenaan were evil in the eyes of Izhak his father,
28.9: went to Ishmael, and took Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael bar Abraham, the sister of Nebaioth, over his wives, unto him to wife.
28.10: And Jakob went forth from Beersheva, and went to Haran;
28.11: and he arrived at a place, and lodged there, because the sun had gone. And he took of the stones of the place, and set his pillow, and lay down in that place.
28.12: And he dreamed: and, behold, a ladder was planted in the earth, and the head of it reached unto the height of heaven; and, behold, the angels of the Lord ascended and descended upon it;
28.13: and, behold, the Glory of the Lord stood above it, and He said, I am the God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Izhak. The land where thou sleepest, unto thee will I give it, and unto thy sons.
28.14: And thy sons shall be many as the dust of the earth, and shall prevail to the west and to the east, and to the north and to the south; and through thee shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed, and through thy sons.
28.15: And, behold, My Word shall be for thy help, and I will keep thee in every place whither thou goest, and I will bring thee again to this land; for I will not leave thee until I have done what I say to thee.
28.16: And Jakob awoke from his sleep, and said, Verily the Glory of the Lord dwelleth in this place, and I knew it not.
28.17: And he feared and said, How awful is this place! This place is not common (ground), but a place where there is pleasantness before the Lord; and this is nigh the gate of heaven.
28.18: And Jakob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone which he had set for his pillow, and set it up, a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.
28.19: And he called the name of that place The House of God (Bethel). But Luz was the name of the city at the first.
28.20: And Jakob vowed a vow, saying, If the Word of the Lord will be my help, and will keep me in that way in which I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to wear,
28.21: and bring me again in peace to the Lord shall be my God.
28.22: And at this stone which I have set up (as) a pillar, will I worship before the Lord; and of all that Thou shalt give me, the tenth will I separate before Thee.

29.1: And Jakob lifted up his feet, and came to the land of the children of the East.
29.2: And he looked, and saw a well in a field; and, behold, three flocks of sheep lying near it, because from that well they watered the flocks; and a great stone was upon the mouth of the well.
29.3: And thither all the flocks were gathered together; and they withdrew the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the flock, and returned the stone upon the mouth of the well unto its place.
29.4: And Jakob said to them, My brethren, whence are you? And they said, We are from Haran.
29.5: And Jakob said to them, Know you Laban bar Nachor? And they said, We know.
29.6: And he said, Hath he peace? And they said, Peace; and, behold, Rahel his daughter cometh with the flock.
29.7: And he said, Behold, the day is yet great, it is not time to gather the cattle; water the sheep, and go to the pasture.
29.8: And they said, We cannot till all the flocks are gathered, and we remove the stone from the mouth of the well, and water the flock.
29.9: While he spake with them, Rahel came, with the flock of her father; for she was a shepherdess.
29.10: And it was, when Jakob saw Rahel the daughter of Laban, the brother of his mother, and the flock of Laban the brother of his mother, that Jakob went near, and withdrew the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban, his mother’s brother.
29.11: And Jakob kissed Rahel, and lifted up his voice and wept.
29.12: And Jakob showed Rahel that he was the son of her father’s sister, and that he was the son of Revekah. And she ran and showed to her father.
29.13: And it was when Laban heard the hearing of Jakob the son of his sister, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him into his house; and he narrated to Laban all these words.
29.14: And Laban said to him, Thou art, however, my near (kinsman), and thou art my flesh. And he abode with him a month of days.
29.15: And Laban said to Jakob, Because thou art my brother, shalt thou serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall be thy wages?
29.16: And Laban had two daughters, the name of the elder Leah, and the name of the younger Rahel.
29.17: And the eyes of Leah were beautiful; but Rahel was admirable in form, and beautiful in aspect.
29.18: And Jakob loved Rahel, and he said, I will serve thee seven years for Rahel thy younger daughter.
29.19: And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee than give her to another man; reside with me.
29.20: And Jakob served for Rahel seven years; and they were in his eyes as a few days, inasmuch as he loved her.
29.21: And Jakob said to Laban, Give me my wife; for the days of my service are fulfilled, and I will go to her.
29.22: And Laban assembled all the men of the place, and made a feast.
29.23: And it was in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and introduced her to him, and he entered to her.
29.24: And Laban gave her Zilpha his handmaid unto Leah his daughter, to attend on her.
29.25: And it was in the morning, and, behold, she was Leah! And he said to Laban, What is this that thou hast done to me? Was it not for Rahel that I served thee? And why hast thou been false with me?
29.26: And Laban said, It is not so done in our place, to give the younger before the elder.
29.27: Fulfil this week, and I will give thee also that, for the service that thou shalt serve with me yet seven other years.
29.28: And Jakob did so, and fulfilled the week of this; and he gave him Rahel his daughter to be his wife.
29.29: And Laban gave to Rahel his daughter Bilhah her handmaid to wait upon her.
29.30: And he went in also to Rahel, and he loved Rahel more than Leah. And he served yet with him seven other years.
29.31: And the Lord saw that Leah was hated, and He gave her to conceive, but Rahel was barren.
29.32: And Leah conceived and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben; for she said, Because my affliction was manifest before the Lord; for now will my husband love me.
29.33: And she conceived again and bare a son, and she said, Because it was heard before the Lord that I had hatred, and He gave me this also; and she called his name Shemeon.
29.34: And she conceived again and bare a son: and she said, This time will my husband adhere to me; for I have born him three sons: therefore she called his name Levi.
29.35: And she conceived again and bare a son; and she said, This time will I give praise before the Lord: therefore she called his name Jehudah. And she ceased (stood) from bearing.

30.1: And Rahel saw that she did not bear unto Jakob; and Rahel envied her sister, and she said to Jakob, Give me children; and if not, I die.
30.2: And the anger of Jakob was incensed against Rahel, and he said, Why ask of me? Is it not before the Lord that thou shouldest ask, who hath denied thee the generation of the womb?
30.3: And she said, Behold my handmaid Bilhah, go in unto her, and she shall bear, and I also shall nourish (children), and be builded up from her.
30.4: And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to wife; and Jakob went in unto her,
30.5: and Bilhah conceived, and bare to Jakob a son.
30.6: And Rahel said, The Lord hath judged me, and hath also received my prayer, and given me a son: therefore she called his name Dan.
30.7: And Bilhah the handmaid of Rahel conceived again, and bare a second son to Jakob.
30.8: And Rahel said, The Lord hath received my request: when I entreated in my prayer, I desired that I might have offspring as my sister, and also it is given me. And she called his name Naphtali.
30.9: And Leah saw that she had ceased from bearing, and she took Zilpha her handmaid, and gave her to Jakob to wife.
30.10: And Zilpha the handmaid of Leah bare a son to Jakob,
30.11: and Leah said, There cometh prosperity; and she called his name Gad.
30.12: And Zilpha the handmaid of Leah bare a second son to Jakob;
30.13: And Leah said, Praise shall be mine; now will women praise me; and she called his name Asher.
30.14: And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and he brought them to Leah his mother. And Rahel said to Leah, Give me now of thy son’s mandrakes.
30.15: And she said to her, Is it a little that thou hast taken my husband, and thou wilt take also my son’s mandrakes? And Rahel said, Therefore shall he lie with thee at night for thy son’s mandrakes.
30.16: And Jakob came in from the field at evening, and Leah went out to anticipate him, and said, With me thou wilt go in, because with hire have I hired thee, with the mandrakes of my son; and he lay with her that night.
30.17: And the Lord received the prayer of Leah, and she conceived, and bare to Jakob a fifth son.
30.18: And Leah said, The Lord hath given me my reward, because I gave my handmaid to my husband. And she called his name Issakar.
30.19: And Leah conceived again, and bare a sixth son to Jakob.
30.20: And Leah said, The Lord hath given me a good portion. This time will the habitation of my husband be with me, because I have born him six sons: therefore she called his name Zebulon.
30.21: And afterward she bare a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
30.22: And the remembrance of Rahel came before the Lord, and the Lord received her prayer, and gave her to conceive.
30.23: And she conceived and bare a son, and she said, The Lord hath taken up my reproach.
30.24: And she called his name Joseph, saying, The Lord shall add to me another son.
30.25: And it was when Rahel had born Joseph, that Jakob said to Laban, Send me away, that I may go to my place, and to my land.
30.26: Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee, that I may go: for thou knowest the service with which I have served thee.
30.27: And Laban said to him, If now I have found grace in thine eyes, I have proved that the Lord hath blessed me for thy sake.
30.28: And he said, Certify thy wages with me, and I will give.
30.29: And he said to him, Thou knowest how I have served thee, and what thy flocks have been with me;
30.30: For thou hadst few before me, and they have increased into a multitude: and the Lord hath blessed thee for my sake. But now, what shall I do also for my (own) house?
30.31: And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me anything; but if thou wilt do with me this matter, I will return, and, pasturing thy flocks, will keep (them).
30.32: I will pass through all thy flocks today, and set apart from them every lamb streaked and speckled, and every black lamb among the lambs, and the streaked and speckled among the goats, and they shall be my wages.
30.33: And my righteousness shall be testified in the day following, when thou wilt come upon my reward that shall be before thee: everyone which is not streaked or speckled among the goats, and black among the lambs, that shall be (as if) stolen by me.
30.34: And Laban said, Let it be according to thy word.
30.35: And he set apart that day the he goats of various colour, and all the goats which were speckled or spotted, everyone which had (some) white in him, and all that were black among the lambs: and he gave them into the hand of his sons.
30.36: And he set a walk of three days between them and Jakob; and Jakob pastured the flock of Laban which remained.
30.37: And Jakob took to him rods of white poplars, and of almond, (or hazel,) and of plane tree, and peeled in them white peelings, (so that, where) peeled, the white which was in the rods appeared.
30.38: And he fixed the rods that he had peeled in the canals, in the place of the watering of waters, the place to which they brought the flocks to drink, to be over against the flocks, that they might be incited when they came to drink.
30.39: And the sheep were incited before the rods, and the sheep brought forth with chequered feet and streaked.
30.40: And Jakob separated the lambs, and set before the sheep which were various coloured and all that were black among the sheep of Laban; and placed them for himself a flock apart, not mixing them with the sheep of Laban.
30.41: And it was that whenever the early (prime) sheep conceived, Jakob placed the rods before the eyes of the sheep in the canals, that they might conceive before the rods: but before the late sheep he did not place them.
30.42: And (so) the late ones were Laban’s, and the prime ones Jacob’s.
30.43: And the man increased very greatly, and had a multitude of flocks, and handmaids, and servants, and camels, and asses.

31.1: And he heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, Jacob hath taken all that was our father’s; and of that which was our father’s he hath gotten all these possessions.
31.2: And Jakob saw the looks of Laban, and, behold, they were not with him as yesterday, and the time before.
31.3: And the Lord said to Jacob, Return to thy country and to thy native (place): and My Word shall be for thy help.
31.4: And Jacob sent and called Rahel and Leah to the field with his flocks:
31.5: And he said to them, I see the looks of your father, that they are not with me as yesterday and the time before; and the God of my father hath been to my help.
31.6: And you know that with all my strength I have served your father;
31.7: But your father hath lied to me, and hath changed my wages ten times; but the Lord hath not permitted him to hurt me.
31.8: If now he said, The streaked shall be thy wages; then all the flock bare streaked: and if now he said, The chequered shall be thy wages; all the flock bare chequered.
31.9: And the Lord hath separated them from the cattle of your father, and hath given (them) to me.
31.10: And it was at the time when the flocks conceived, I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream, and, behold, the rams which leaped upon the flock were chequered, streaked, and speckled.
31.11: And the angel of the Lord said to me in a dream, Jacob. And I said, Behold, I am.
31.12: And he said, Lift up now thine eyes, and see, all the rams which leap upon the flock are chequered, streaked, and speckled: because all that Laban hath done to thee is manifest before Me.
31.13: I am Eloha, who appeared to thee at Bethel, where thou didst anoint the pillar, and where before Me thou didst swear the oath: arise now, go from this land, and return to the land of thy birth.
31.14: And Rahel and Leah answered and said to him, Have we yet a portion or inheritance in our father’s house?
31.15: Are we not accounted as strangers by him? For he hath sold us, and hath devoured our money also.
31.16: Therefore, all the wealth that the Lord hath separated from our father is ours and our children’s: and now all that the Lord hath said to thee, do.
31.17: And Jakob arose, and lifted up his sons and his wives upon camels;
31.18: And led all his herds and all his substance which he had obtained, his herds and his substance which he had obtained in Padan Aram, to go unto Izhak his father in the land of Kenaan.
31.19: And Laban had gone to shear his flock: and Rahel took the images that were her father’s.
31.20: And Jakob concealed from Laban the Aramite, and showed him not that he went.
31.21: And he went, he and all that were his; and he arose and passed the Phrat, and set his face toward the mountain of Gilead.
31.22: And it was shown to Laban on the third day that Jakob had gone.
31.23: And he took his brethren with him, and Pursued after him; going seven days; and he overtook him in the Mountain of Gilead.
31.24: And a word came from before the Lord to Laban the Aramite in a dream of the night, and He said to him, Beware, lest thou speak with Jakob from good to evil.
31.25: And Laban overtook Jakob; and Jakob had spread his tent in the mountain; and Laban made his brethren abide in the mountain of Gilead.
31.26: And Laban said to Jacob; What hast thou done, that thou hast hidden from me, and taken away my daughters, as captives of the sword?
31.27: Why didst thou conceal thy going, (or conceal thyself to go,) and didst hide it from me, and not show me, that I might then have sent thee away with mirth, and with hymns, and with tambourines, and with harps?
31.28: Nor didst thou suffer me to kiss my sons and my daughters. Now hast thou done foolishly.
31.29: It is in the power of my bands to do evil with thee: but the God of thy father spake to me in the evening, saying, Beware lest thou speak to Jakob from good to evil.
31.30: And now, (though) going thou wouldest go, because desiring thou bast desired the house of thy father, why hast thou taken my religion?
31.31: And Jakob answered and said to Laban, Because I feared; for I said, Lest thou shouldst take away thy daughters from me.
31.32: The place where thou shalt find thy religious things shall not abide: before our brethren ascertain thou what of thine is with me, and take to thee. But Jakob knew not that Rahel had carried them away.
31.33: And Laban entered into the tent of Leah, and into the tent of the two concubines, but found not; and he went forth from the tent of Leah, and entered the tent of Rahel.
31.34: But Rahel had taken the images, and laid them in the panniers of the camels, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found not.
31.35: And she said to her father, Let it not be displeasing in the eyes of my lord, that I am not able to rise before thee; for the way of women is upon me. And he scrutinized, but found not the images.
31.36: And Jakob was angry, and contended with Laban. And Jakob answered and said to Laban, What is my guilt, my crime, that thou hast pursued after me?
31.37: Now that thou hast searched all my things, what hast thou found, of all the things of thy house? Set it here before my brethren and thy brethren, and they shall decide between us both.
31.38: These twenty years have I been with thee; thy ewes and thy goats have not failed, and the rams of thy flock I have not eaten.
31.39: The wounded I have not brought to thee; what was deficient in number, from my hand hast thou required it. I have watched by day, and I have watched by night.
31.40: (Thus) have I been; in the day the heat devoured me, and the frost came down upon me at night, and sleep passed away from my eyes.
31.41: These twenty years have I served in thy house; fourteen years for thy two daughters; and six years for thy sheep; and thou hast changed my wages ten times.
31.42: Unless the God of my fathers, the God of Abraham, and He whom Izhak hath feared, had been my helper, even now thou hadst sent me away empty: but my labour, and the travail of my hands, have been manifest before the Lord, and He rebuked thee in the evening.
31.43: And Laban answered and said to Jakob, The daughters are my daughters, and the sons my sons, and the sheep are my sheep, and all whatsoever thou seest is mine; and to these, my daughters, what can I do this day, or unto their children which they have born?
31.44: And now come, let us enter into a covenant, I and thou, and it shall be for a witness between me and thee.
31.45: And Jakob took a stone, and set it up as a pillar.
31.46: And Jakob said to his brethren, Collect stones; and they took stones, and made a mound, and ate there upon the mound.
31.47: And Laban called it Yegar Sahadutha, but Jakob called it Gal-Ed.
31.48: And Laban said, This mound testifieth between me and thee today.
31.49: Therefore he called the name of it The Heap of Witness, and The Observatory; for he said, The Word of the Lord will observe between me and thee, when we are hidden each man from his neighbor.
31.50: If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take wives over my daughters, no man is with us; see, the Word of the Lord is witness between me and thee.
31.51: And Laban said to Jakob, Behold this mound and this pillar, which thou bast erected between me and thee.
31.52: And Laban said, This mound testifieth between me and thee today. And Laban said, This mound testifieth between me and thee today. This mound and pillar are a witness, that I will not pass over this mound to thee; and that thou shalt not pass over this mound and this pillar, to do me evil.
31.53: The God of Abraham and the God of Nachor shall judge between us, the God of their fathers. And Jakob sware by Him whom Izhak his father feared.
31.54: And Jakob sacrificed victims in the mountain, and called his brethren to eat bread; and they ate bread, and tabernacled in the mountain.

32.1: And Laban arose in the morning, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them, and went; and Laban returned to his place.
32.2: And Jakob went on his way, and the angels of the Lord met him.
32.3: And when Jakob saw them, he said, This is a host from before the Lord; and he called the name of the place Mahanaim.
32.4: And Jakob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother to the land of Seir, in the region of Edom;
32.5: And he instructed them, saying, So shall you tell to my lord, to Esau: Thus saith thy servant Jakob, With Laban I have dwelt, and have tarried, until now.
32.6: And I have oxen, and asses, sheep, and servants, and handmaids, and have sent to show my lord, to find grace in thine eyes.
32.7: And the messengers returned to Jakob, saying, We came to thy brother, to Esau; and he cometh also to meet thee, and four hundred men with him.
32.8: And Jakob feared greatly, and it distressed him. And he divided the people that were with him, and the sheep, and oxen, and camels, into two hosts,
32.9: And said, If Esau come to the one host and smite it, the host that is left may escape.
32.10: And Jakob said, God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Izhak, the Lord, who didst say to me, Return to thy country and to thy native place, and I will do thee good;
32.11: less are my righteousnesses than all the mercies and all the benefits which Thou hast performed unto Thy servant: for alone I passed this Yardena, and now I have become two bands.
32.12: Deliver me now from the hand of my brother, from the band of Esau; for I am afraid of him, lest he come and smite me, and the mother with the children.
32.13: And Thou hast said, In doing good I will do good with thee, and will make thy sons many as the sand of the sea which cannot be numbered for number.
32.14: And he housed there that night, and took of that which came to his hand, an offering for Esau his brother;
32.15: Goats two hundred, rams twenty, ewes two hundred, and rams twenty,
32.16: Camels giving milk and their young ones thirty, cows forty, and bulls ten, she-asses twenty, and colts ten.
32.17: And he gave them into the hand of his servants, herd by herd separately, and said to his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space between herd and herd.
32.18: And he commanded the foremost, saying, If Esau my brother meet thee, and ask thee, saying, Whose art thou? And, Whither goest thou? And, Whose are these that are before thee?
32.19: Thou shalt say, They are an offering of thy servant Jakob, which he hath sent to my lord, to Esau; and, behold, he also cometh after us.
32.20: And he instructed also the second and the third, and all of them who followed the herds, saying, According to this word you shall speak with Esau, when you find him;
32.21: And say also, Behold, thy servant Jakob cometh after. For he said, I will quiet his anger by the offering that goeth before me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will accept me.
32.22: And the offering went over before his face, and he himself lodged that night in the camp.
32.23: And he arose in the night, and took his two wives, and his two concubines, and his eleven sons, and passed over the ford Jubeka;
32.24: And he took them and made them pass over the torrent, and made what was his to pass over.
32.25: And Jakob remained alone; and a Man wrestled with him till the morning ascended.
32.26: And he saw that he prevailed not with him, and he touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was dislocated in wrestling with him.
32.27: And he said, Let me go; for the morning ascendeth And he said, I will not let Thee go, unless Thou bless me.
32.28: And He said to him, What is thy name? And he said, Jakob.
32.29: And He said, Thy name shall be no longer Jakob, but Israel; for a prince art thou before the Lord, and with men, and thou hast prevailed.
32.30: And Jakob asked Him, and said, Show me now Thy Name! And He said, Why dost thou ask My Name? And He blessed him there.
32.31: And Jakob called the name of the place Peniel: because I have seen the Angel of the Lord face to face, and my soul hath been saved!
32.32: And the sun arose upon him as he passed over Penuel, and he went lame upon his thigh.
32.33: Therefore the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew which shrank, which is upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day, because He touched the hollow of Jakob’s thigh in the sinew that shrank.

33.1: And Jakob lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men; and he divided the children with Leah, and with Rahel, and with the two concubines.
33.2: And he set the concubines and their children first, and Leah and her children after, and Rahel and Joseph after them.
33.3: And he passed over before them, and bowed to the earth seven times, until he came nigh to his brother.
33.4: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell upon his neck, and kissed him; and they wept.
33.5: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children, and said, What are these to thee? And he said, The children whom the Lord hath given to thy servant.
33.6: And the concubines approached, they and their children, and bowed.
33.7: And Leah also approached and her children, and bowed; and afterward Joseph and Rahel approached, and bowed.
33.8: And he said, What to thee is all this troop which I have met? And he said, To find mercy in the eyes of my lord.
33.9: And Esau said, I have much, my brother; let what is thine own profit thee.
33.10: And Jakob said, I pray thee, if I have now found mercy in thine eyes, that thou wouldst accept the present from my hand, because I have now seen thy face as the vision of the face of the Great, and thou art pleased with me.
33.11: Receive, I pray, my offering which is brought to thee, because the Lord hath been merciful to me, and because I have all.
33.12: And he was urgent on him, and he took it. And he said, Let us journey and go, and I will go along with thee.
33.13: And he said, My lord knoweth that the little ones are tender, and the sheep and kine giving milk are with me; and if they overdrive them one day, all the flock may die.
33.14: Let my lord pass on before his servant, and I will lead on quietly, according to the foot of the little ones, according to the foot of the work that is before me, and according to the foot of the sucklings, until I come to my lord at Seir.
33.15: And Esau said, Let me leave with thee of the people who are with me. And he said, Why should this be? Let me find grace in the eyes of my lord.
33.16: And Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
33.17: And Jakob journeyed to Succoth, and builded him an house, and made tabernacles for his cattle; therefore he called the name of the place Succoth.
33.18: And Jakob came in peace to the city of Shekem, which is in the land of Kenaan, in his coming from Padan Aram, and he abode near the face of the city.
33.19: And he bought the possession of the field where he had spread his tent, of the hand of the sons of Hamor, the father of Shekem, for a hundred lambs.
33.20: And he raised there an altar, and offered service upon it before God, the God of Israel.

34.1: And Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she bare to Jakob, went forth to see the daughters of the land.
34.2: And Shekem bar Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her, and took her, and lay with her, and humbled her.
34.3: And his soul took pleasure in Dinah the daughter of Jakob, and he loved the damsel, and spake to the heart of the damsel.
34.4: And Shekem spake to Hamor his father, saying, Take to me this damsel for a wife.
34.5: And Jakob heard that he had polluted Dinah his daughter. And his sons were with his flocks in the field; and Jakob was silent until they were come.
34.6: And Hamor the father of Shekem came forth to Jakob to speak with him.
34.7: And the sons of Jakob came up from the field when they heard. And the men were indignant and very angry, because shame had been wrought in Israel by his lying with the daughter of Jacob; for so it should not have been done.
34.8: Hamor spake with them, saying, The soul of Shekem my son hath pleasure in your daughter; give her now to him to wife.
34.9: And marry with us, and take our daughters to you;
34.10: And the land shall be before you; inhabit and do business in it, and possess it.
34.11: And Shekem said to her father and to her brethren, Let me find favour in your eyes, and what you shall tell me I will give.
34.12: Multiply upon me dowry and present, and I will give as you may tell me; but give me the damsel to wife.
34.13: And the sons of Jakob answered Shekem and Hamor his father, and with subtlety they spake, because he had defiled Dinah their sister.
34.14: And they said to them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to a man uncircumcised; for that (would be) a reproach to us.
34.15: Nevertheless in this we will agree with you, if you will be as we are, by circumcising every male among you,
34.16: and we will give our daughters to you, and your daughters will we take to us, and will dwell with you and be one people.
34.17: But if you will not consent to us to be circumcised, we will take our daughter and go.
34.18: And their words were pleasing in the eyes of Hamor, and in the eyes of Shekem the son of Hamor.
34.19: And the young man delayed not to do the thing, because he delighted in the daughter of Jakob, and he was more honourable than all his father’s house.
34.20: And Hamor came, and Shekem his son, to the gate of the city, and spake to the men of the city, saying,
34.21: These men are friendly with us, and they may dwell in the land, and do business in it, and the land, behold, it is wide (on both) hands before them; their daughters we will take to us for wives, and our daughters we will give to them.
34.22: Only in this will the men agree with us to dwell with us, to be one people, in every male of us being circumcised, as they are circumcised.
34.23: Their flocks, and their possessions, and all their cattle, will they not be ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell with us.
34.24: And everyone who went out of the gate of his city received of Hamor and of Shekem his son, and they were circumcised, every male, everyone who went out of the gate of his city.
34.25: And it was on the third day, when their pains were strong upon them, that the two sons of Jakob, Shemeon and Levi, the brothers of Dinah, took each man his sword, and came upon the city, which dwelt in security, and slew every male,
34.26: and Hamor and Shekem his son they killed with the edge of the sword. And they brought Dinah out of the house of Shekem, and went.
34.27: And the sons of Jakob came up to the spoil of the slain, and sacked the town, because they had defiled their sister.
34.28: Their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses, and all that was in the city and the field, they took.
34.29: And all their substance, and all their little ones, and their wives, they captured and spoiled, and all which was in the house.
34.30: And Jakob said to Shemeon and Levi, You have troubled me, in putting strife between me and the inhabitants of the land, the Kenaanites and the Perrezites, and I a people (few) for number; and they will gather against me, and smite me, and I shall perish, I and the men of my house.
34.31: And they said, As with an outcast should he deal with our sister?

35.1: And the Lord said to Jakob, Arise, go up to Bethel, and dwell there, and make there an altar unto Eloha, who appeared to thee when in thy flight from before Esau thy brother.
35.2: And Jakob said to the men of his house, and to all who were with him, Put away the gentile idols that are among you, and purify; and change your raiment;
35.3: And we will arise and go up to Bethel, and I will make there an altar unto Eloha, who heard my prayer in the day of my distress, and whose Word was my helper in the way that I went.
35.4: And they gave Jakob all the gentile idols that were in their hands, and the jewels that were in their ears, and Jakob hid them under the terebinth which was near Shekem.
35.5: And they journeyed; and fear from before the Lord was upon the peoples in the cities surrounding them; and they followed not after the sons of Jakob.
35.6: And Jakob came to Luz, which is in the land of Kenaan, which is Bethel, he and all the people who were with him.
35.7: And he builded there an altar, and called the place El Bethel, because the Angel of the Lord had appeared to him there when he fled from before his brother.
35.8: And Deborah, the nurse of Revekah, died, and was buried below Bethel, in the declivity of the vale; and he called the name of it, The vale of weeping.
35.9: And the Lord appeared unto Jakob again when he had come from Padan Aram, and blessed him.
35.10: And the Lord said to Jakob, Thy name shall be no more Jakob, but Israel shall be thy name; and he called his name Israel.
35.11: And the Lord said to him, I am El Shadai; increase and multiply; a people and an assemblage of tribes shall be from thee, and kings who shall reign over the peoples shall come forth from thee.
35.12: And the land that I gave to Abraham and to Izhak I will give unto thee, and to thy sons after thee, will I give the land.
35.13: And the glory of the Lord ascended above him, in the place where He had spoken with him.
35.14: And Jakob erected a pillar in the place where He had spoken with him, a pillar of stone, and outpoured libations upon it, and poured oil thereon.
35.15: And Jakob called the name of the place where the Lord bad spoken with him Bethel.
35.16: And they journeyed from Bethel, and there was yet a space of land to come unto Ephrath; and Rahel travailed, and had hard (pain) in her birth-labour.
35.17: And as she travailed in her labour, the midwife said to her, Fear not, for also this to thee is a son.
35.18: And it was in the going forth of her soul, for she died, that she called his name The son of my woe; but his father called him Benjamin.
35.19: And Rahel died, and was buried in the way of Ephrath, which is Beth-Lechem.
35.20: And Jakob erected a pillar upon her grave: that is the pillar of the tomb of Rahel unto this day.
35.21: And Israel proceeded and spread his tabernacle beyond the tower of Adar.
35.22: And it was while Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, the concubine of his father. And Israel heard it. And the sons of Jakob were twelve.
35.23: The sons of Leah, the firstborn of Jakob, Reuben, and Shemeon, and Levi, and Jehudah, and Issakar, and Zebulon.
35.24: The sons of Rahel, Joseph and Benjamin.
35.25: The sons of Bilhah, the handmaid of Rahel, Dan and Naphtali;
35.26: and the sons of Zilpha, the handmaid of Leah, Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jakob, who were born to him in Padan Aram.
35.27: And Jakob came unto Izhak his father, unto Mamre, the city of Arba, which is Hebron; for Abraham and Izhak had dwelt there.
35.28: And the days of Izhak were an hundred and eighty years.
35.29: And Izhak expired and died, and was gathered unto his people, old and content with days; and Esau and Jakob his sons buried him.

36.1: And these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom.
36.2: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Kenaan: Ada, daughter of Helon the Hittite, and Ahalivama, the daughter of Ana, the daughter of Sibeon the Hivite,
36.3: and Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebaioth.
36.4: And Ada bare to Esau Eliphaz; and Basemath bare Reuel;
36.5: and Ahalivama bare Jehus, and Jaalam, and Korach. These are the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Kenaan.
36.6: And Esau took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the souls of his house, and his flocks, and all his cattle, and all his substance which he had gotten in the land of Kenaan, and went into another land from before Jakob his brother;
36.7: Because their substance was too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their habitation could not sustain them with regard to their cattle.
36.8: And Esau dwelt in the mountain of Seir. Esau is Edom.
36.9: And these are the generations of Esau, the father of the Edomai, in the mountain of Seir,
36.10: these are the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz, the son of Ada, the wife of Esau; Reuel, son of Basemath, the wife of Esau.
36.11: And the sons of Eliphaz were Theman, Omar, Zepho, and Gaetam, and Kenaz.
36.12: And Thimna was the concubine of Eliphaz bar Esau, and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek. These are the sons of Ada, the wife of Esau.
36.13: And these are the sons of Reuel, Nahath and Zara, Shamma and Meza. These are the sons of Basemath, the wife of Esau.
36.14: And these are the sons of Ahalivama, the daughter of Ana, the daughter of Zebeon, the wife of Esau; and she bare unto Esau Jehus, and Jaalam, and Korach.
36.15: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau. Of the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau, Rabba Theman, Rabba Omar, Rabba Zepho, Rabba Kenaz,
36.16: rabba Korach, Rabba Gaetam, Rabba Amalek These are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Ada.
36.17: And these are the sons of Reuel bar Esau: Rabba Nachath, Rabba Zarach, Rabba Shamma, Rabba Meza. These are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, the wife of Esau.
36.18: And these are the sons of Ahalivama, the wife of Esau: Rabba Jehus, Rabba Jaalam, Rabba Korach. These are the chiefs of Ahalivama, the daughter of Ana the wife of Esau.
36.19: These are the sons of Esau, and these are their chieftains. He is Edom.
36.20: These are the sons of Seir, the Chorites, the inhabitants of the land, Lothan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Ana,
36.21: and Dishon, and Etser, and Dishan. These are the chieftains of the Choraai, the sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
36.22: And the sons of Loti were Hori and Hemaim, and the sister of Lotan was Timna.
36.23: And these are the Beni Shobal, Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shephi, and Onam.
36.24: And these are the sons of Zebeon, Aya and Ana; he is Ana who found the giants in the desert while he tended the asses of his father Zibeon.
36.25: And these are the children of Ana, Dishon, and Ahalivania the daughter of Ana.
36.26: And these are the sons of Dishan: Hemdan, and Eshban, and Jethran, and Keran.
36.27: These are the sons of Etser: Bilan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
36.28: These are the sons of Dishan: Huts and Aran.
36.29: These are the chieftains of the Choraai: Rabba Lotan, Rabba Shobal, Rabba Zebeon, Rabba Ana,
36.30: Rabba Dishon, Rabba Etser, Rabba Dishan. These are the chieftains of the Choraai, according to their principalities in the land of Seir.
36.31: And these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before that kings reigned among the sons of Israel:
36.32: Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhava.
36.33: And Bela died, and instead of him reigned Yobab the son of Zerah of Botsra.
36.34: And Yobab died, and instead of him reigned Husham, of the land of the south.
36.35: And Husham, died, and instead of him reigned Hadad, the son of Bedad, who slew the Medianae in the fields of Moab; and the name of his city was Avith.
36.36: And Hadad died, and in his stead reigned Simlah of Masereka.
36.37: And Simlah died, and in his stead reigned Shaul of Rechovoth, which is on the Ph’rat.
36.38: And Shaul died, and in his stead reigned Baal-Chanan bar Akbor.
36.39: And Baal-Chanan bar Akbor died, and in his stead reigned Hadar, and the name of his city was, Pau; and the name of his wife Mehetavel, the daughter of Matered, the daughter of a changer of gold.
36.40: And these are the names of the chieftains of Esau, after their kindreds, by their places, with their names: Rabba Timna, Rabba Alvah, Rabba Jetheth,
36.41: Rabba Ahalivama, Rabba Elah, Rabba Phinon,
36.42: Rabba Kenez, Rabba Teman, Rabba Mabzar,
36.43: Rabba Magdiel, Rabba Iram: these are the chieftains of Edom, after their habitations in the land of their possessions. He is Esau, the father of the Edomites.

37.1: And Jakob dwelt in the land of the habitation of his father, in the land of Kenaan.
37.2: These are the generations of Jakob. Joseph was a son of seventeen years; he kept the flock with his brothers; and he had been brought up with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpha, the wives of his father; and Joseph brought their evil report to his father.
37.3: But Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he had in him a wise son, and he made him a variegated robe.
37.4: And his brothers saw that their father loved him better than all his brethren, and they hated him, and were not willing to speak with him peaceably.
37.5: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and showed it to his brothers, and they hated him the more.
37.6: And he said to them, Hear now this dream which I have dreamed:
37.7: Behold, we were binding sheaves in the midst of the field, and lo! My sheaf arose and became upright, and, behold, your sheaves stood around and worshipped my sheaf.
37.8: And his brothers said to him, Is it thy fancy reigning to reign over us? Or a shultan, dost thou think to govern us? And they added yet to hate him for his dreams and for his words.
37.9: And he dreamed yet another dream, and described it to his brothers, saying, Behold, I have dreamed a dream again; and lo, the sun, and the moon, and eleven stars worshipped me.
37.10: And he described it to his father and to his brethren; and his father rebuked him and said to him, What dream is this that thou hast dreamed? Am I and thy mother and thy brothers to come and worship thee on the earth?
37.11: And his brothers envied him; but his father kept the word.
37.12: And his brothers went to tend the flock of their father in Shekem.
37.13: And Israel said to Joseph, Do not thy brothers tend the flock in Shekem? Come, I will send thee to them. And he said. Behold me.
37.14: And he said to him, Go now, and see the welfare of your brothers and the welfare of the flock, and return me word. And he sent him from the vale of Hebron, and he came to Shekem.
37.15: And a man found him, and, behold, he wandered in the field. And the man inquired of him, saying, Whom seekest thou?
37.16: And he said, I look for my brothers: show me, I beseech thee, where they feed.
37.17: And the man said, They have gone hence; for I heard them say, We will go to Dothan. And Joseph went after his brethren, and found them in Dothan.
37.18: And they saw him from afar; and before he came nigh, they devised against him to kill him.
37.19: And they said, a man to his brother, Behold, this master of dreams cometh.
37.20: And now, come, we will kill him, and cast him into one of the pits; and will say an evil beast hath devoured him, and we shall see what will be the end of his dreams.
37.21: And Reuben heard, and delivered him out of their hands, and said, Let us not slay his life.
37.22: And Reuben said, Do not shed blood; cast him into this pit in the wilderness, but stretch not forth a hand against him, that he might deliver him from their hands to bring him back to his father.
37.23: And it was when Joseph had come to his brethren that they took off his robe, the variegated robe which was upon him,
37.24: And they took him and cast him into the pit; but the pit was empty, no water was in it.
37.25: And they reclined to eat bread. And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a band of Arabaee were coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing spices, and resin, and myrrh, to go down to Mizraim.
37.26: And Jehuda said to his brethren, What gain should we have by killing our brother and covering his blood?
37.27: Come, and we will sell him to the Arabaee, and our hand shall not be upon him; for he is our brother, our flesh. And his brethren hearkened to him.
37.28: And there passed by Midianite men, (gabree Mid-ya-naee,) merchants, and they drew and lifted up Joseph from the pit, and sold Joseph to the Arabaee for twenty of silver; and they brought Joseph into Mizraim.
37.29: And Reuben returned to the pit, and, behold, Joseph was not in the pit. And he rent his clothes,
37.30: And returned to his brethren, and said, The youth is not; and I, whither shall I go?
37.31: But they took Joseph’s robe, and killed a kid of the goats, and dabbled the robe in the blood.
37.32: And they sent the variegated robe, and they brought to their father, and said, This have we found; know now whether it is the robe of thy son, or not.
37.33: And he knew it, and said, It is my son’s robe; an evil beast hath devoured him: slain, slain is Joseph!
37.34: And Jakob rent his clothes, and wrapped sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
37.35: And all his sons, and all his house, arose to comfort him; but he refused to take comfort, and said, For I will go down unto my son, mourning into Sheol. And his father wept for him.
37.36: And the Midianites sold him in Mizraim to Potiphar, a prince of Pharoh, chief of the killers.

38.1: And it was at that time that Jehuda went down from his brethren, and turned aside to an Adulamite man whose name was Hira.
38.2: And Jehuda saw there the daughter of a merchant man whose name was Shuva, and he took her and went in with her;
38.3: And she conceived and bare a son, and he called his name Her;
38.4: And she conceived again, and bare a son, and called his name Onan.
38.5: And she added again, and bare a son, and called his name Shelah; and he was in Kezib when she bare him.
38.6: And Jehuda took a wife for Her his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
38.7: And Her the firstborn of Jehuda was evil before the Lord, and the Lord caused him to die.
38.8: And Jehuda said to Onan, Go in with the wife of thy brother, and associate with her, and raise up seed to thy brother.
38.9: And Onan knew that after his name the seed would not be called; and it was that when he went in with the wife of his brother, he corrupted his way upon the earth that he might not raise up seed unto his brother;
38.10: And what he did was evil before the Lord, and he caused him also to die.
38.11: And Jehuda said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, Remain a widow in thy father’s house until Shelah my son be grown up. For he said, Lest he also die like his brothers: and Tamar went and dwelt in her father’s house.
38.12: And after many days the daughter of Shuva, Jehuda’s wife, died: and Jehuda was comforted; and he went up to the shearers of his sheep, he and Hira the Adulamite his friend unto Timnath.
38.13: And it was shown to Tamar, saying, Behold, thy father-in-law cometh to Timnath to shear his sheep.
38.14: And she laid aside the dress of her widowhood, and covered herself with a mantle (or a large veil), and adorned herself, and sat in the dividing of Aynin which is in the way to Timnath. For she saw that Shelah had grown up, and she had not been given to him for a wife.
38.15: And Jehuda saw her, and thought that she was an outcast, because she had covered her face.
38.16: And he declined to her by the way, and said, Give me now to go in unto thee; for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, What wilt thou give me, that thou mayest come to me?
38.17: And he said, I will send thee a kid of the goats from the flock. And she said, If thou wilt give me a pledge until thou send.
38.18: And he said, What is the pledge that I shall give thee? And she said, Thy seal-ring, and thy scarf, and thy staff that is in thy hand. And he gave to her, and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
38.19: And she arose, and went, and put off the veil from her, and dressed herself in the dress of her widowhood.
38.20: And Jehuda sent the kid of the goats, by the hand of his friend the Adulamite, to receive the pledge from the hand of the woman; but he could not find her.
38.21: And he inquired of the men of the place, saying, Where is the harlot who was in Aynin upon the way? And they said to him, There is no harlot here.
38.22: And he returned to Jehuda, and said, I could not find her; the men of the place also said there is no harlot there.
38.23: And Jehuda said, Let her take it to her, lest we be in contempt: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.
38.24: And it was three months, and it was showed to Jehuda, saying, Tamar thy daughter-in-law hath committed fornication, and, behold, she is with child by fornication. And Jehuda said, Bring her out, and let her be burned.
38.25: And she was brought out. And she sent to her father-in-law, saying, By the man to whom these belong I am with child. And she said, Acknowledge now, whose are these, the seal, the scarf, and the staff?
38.26: And Jehuda acknowledged and said, She is justified in having conceived from me, because I have not given her Shelah my son. And he added not again to know her.
38.27: And it was the time of her giving birth, and, behold, twins were in her womb.
38.28: And it was in giving birth that one of them put forth a hand; and the midwife took and tied scarlet upon his hand, saying, This came the first.
38.29: And it was when he had drawn back his hand that his brother came forth: and she said, How much greater strength is with thee, that thou hast prevailed! And she called his name Pharets.
38.30: And afterwards came forth his brother who had the crimson on his hand, and she called his name Zarah.

39.1: But Joseph was brought down into Mizraim, and Potiphar, a chief of Pharoh, a chief of the killers, a Mizraite man, bought him from the hand of the Arabaee who had brought him down thither.
39.2: And the Word of the Lord was the helper of Joseph, and he became a prosperous man, and was in the house of his Mizraite master.
39.3: And his master saw that the Word of the Lord was his helper, and that all that he did the Lord prospered in his hand.
39.4: And Joseph found favour in his eyes, and he served him. And he appointed him over his house, and all that he had he delivered into his hand.
39.5: And it was from the time that he appointed him over his house, and over all that he had, that the Lord blessed the house of the Mizraite for Joseph’s sake, and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.
39.6: And he left all that belonged to him in the hand of Joseph; and he knew of nothing that was with him, except the bread which he ate. Now Joseph was of goodly appearance, beautiful in aspect.
39.7: And it was after these things that the wife of his master lifted up her eyes to Joseph, and said, Lie with me.
39.8: But be refused, and said to his master’s wife, Behold, my master knoweth not what is with me in the house, and all that he hath he hath delivered unto my hand;
39.9: There is no one in this housegreater than I, and be hath not prohibited anything from me but thyself, because thou art his wife: and how can I do this great wickedness and become guilty before the Lord?
39.10: And it was when she spake with Joseph daily that he would not hearken to her to lie with her, or be with her.
39.11: And it was about this day that he came into the house to examine the writings of his affairs, and no man of the men of the house was there in the house.
39.12: And she laid hold of his garments, saying, Lie with me. But he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and went forth into the street.
39.14: And she called to the men of her house, and spake to them, saying, See, he brought us a Hebrew man to mock at us. He came in to me to lie with me; and I cried with a high voice.
39.15: And it was when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his robe with me, and fled and went forth into the street.
39.16: And she let his robe remain with her until his master came into his house.
39.17: And she spake with him these words, saying, The Hebrew servant whom thou broughtest us came in to me to mock at me.
39.18: And it was when I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his robe with me and fled into the street.
39.19: And when his master heard the words of his wife which she spake with him, saying, According to these things hath thy servant done to me, his anger waxed strong,
39.20: And his master took Joseph, and delivered him to the house of the bound, where the prisoners of the king were bound; and he was there in the house of the bound.
39.21: But the Word of the Lord was the helper of Joseph, and showed him mercy, and gave him favour in the eyes of the captain of the prison.
39.22: And the captain of the prison gave into the hand of Joseph all the prisoners who were in the house of the bound, and all that they did there was done according to his word.
39.23: The captain of the prison saw no fault in his hand, because the Word of the Lord was his helper, and that which he did the Lord made to prosper.

40.1: And after these things the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Mizraim offended their master, the king of Mizraim.
40.2: And Pharoh was angry with two of his chiefs, with the chief of the cupbearers and with the chief of the bakers.
40.3: And he gave them into ward in the house of the captain of the executioners (killers) in the house of the prison, the place where Joseph was confined.
40.4: And the captain of the executioners appointed Joseph with them, and he ministered to them, and they were certain days inward.
